Estimator: vertices ordered along the principal axis, slabs ~ one diameter thick, per slab the median perpendicular distance to the LOCAL axis (neighbouring slab centres, so a curved vessel is fine) -> 2 x median of the slab medians, cross-checked with lateral area / (pi x centreline length), the smaller of two disagreeing values kept (a branch only inflates the area figure); unit tests on synthetic tubes (r 0.5-12.5 mm within 8 %, an arch within 20 %, a branch stub does not inflate the trunk). Injected into each page as `<script id="nmsk-calibre">{"v":1,"c":{id:[kind,diameter,level,promoted]}}` between `NMSK-CALIBRE begin/end` (next to the abbreviation table; `make_calibre.py --inject DIR`, called by `regen_q240.sh`).

## Q252 (2026-10-16) -- PUDENDAL NERVES FIXED TO STAY IN SKIN, CVH PERINEAL STRUCTURES ON BASE F, BREAST TAPER SMOOTHED (agent; from build/q252/{viewer_base_female,viewer_zan_female,viewer_zan_atlas,viewer_zan_vhm,viewer_f_hr,viewer_m_hr})
Owner (translated): "the pudendal nerve looks like it's outside the body"; "deformities... in the genitalia"; "missing a lot of details". Three separate bugs, found and fixed.
- **(1) Root cause of the "outside the body" nerve.** `scripts/anatomy/q249/rule_nerves.py`'s `min_skin` gate (every nerve) calls `gd.skin_depth()` (q248/guards.py): correct (SIGNED, positive = inside) on the two CT-segmented "own" pages, which carry one closed `skin` mesh, but on the four Z-Anatomy pages (base_f, base_m, comb_f, comb_m) the skin is ~250 separate open regional patches with no single enclosing mesh, so it falls back to an UNSIGNED nearest-point distance there: a waypoint floating tens of mm outside the body in a pocket with no nearby patch (e.g. the widened perineum after Q250's pelvis warp) reads as a large POSITIVE "depth", exactly like a point deep inside -- the gate could never catch it, on any Z page, for any nerve whose candidate end point is a free search with no anchor organ. **Verified empirically**, not just reasoned: reran `run_rule.py` for all six pages and checked every perineal-region nerve's actual waypoints against the page's own skin mesh. `perineal_n`, `inferior_rectal_n` and `anococcygeal_n` were ALL silently shipping 15-56 mm outside the skin on every one of the four Z pages (not only the one nerve the owner noticed) -- `dorsal_n_clitoris` was NOT the bug (correctly held already, "no clitoris on the page", per Q249). Two more candidate "general" fixes were tried and rejected because they produced false holds on nerves that were already fine (`lumbosacral_trunk_l` read ~85 mm outside skin when it was actually ~85 mm inside, from a single mis-wound patch getting the majority global sign, or from the thin-shell inner/outer layer ambiguity of a per-mesh volume-sign orientation) -- full reasoning for both rejected attempts is kept in the code's own docstrings (`Builder._skin_envelope`) so the next person does not re-try them. The fix that held up: scoped to `region="perineum"` nerves only (exactly the class of nerve the task is about, and the only one with no anchor organ to rely on), checked only on the distal 40% of the centreline (the proximal canal part is legitimately deep and would misread against a sparse local patch set), against a small, hand-verified set of LOCAL perineal skin patches (name-matched: perineal_closure, anal_region, gluteal_fold/region, femoral_triangle, labia/mons/scrotum/groin/genital keywords), using their RAW (unflipped) winding -- confirmed correct by a direct per-face offset test on every one of them. Also made the candidate search for `perineal_n`'s terminal branch skin-aware (`best_end(..., skin=True)`): when the documented direction family offers an in-skin candidate it is now preferred over a bone-only-optimal one; when none exists, the nerve is honestly held (same `B.hold` pattern already used for a missing anchor organ).
- **(2) CVH perineal structures on Base F -- why the guard failed, and what was and wasn't fixable.** `scripts/zanatomy/q235_z_female.py` had an all-or-nothing rule for base_f only: if ANY of 4 bone-attached CVH structures (`clitoris_cavernous_body`, both `ischiocavernosus_cvh`, `bulbospongiosus_cvh`) failed its own gate, NOTHING was added to the page at all -- even though the per-structure gates (`core.evaluate()`) already compute pass/fail individually, and every OTHER page (own_f, comb_f) ships per-structure as normal. On TODAY's Q250-warped pelvis (inferior-pelvis residual median down to about 2.3-2.7 mm / p90 6.5-6.8 mm, from 3.1 / 8.4 mm on the old male-derived pelvis): both `ischiocavernosus_cvh_l/r` now genuinely PASS outright; `bulbospongiosus_cvh` fails only a conservative "must clear bone by >= 1.0 mm" gate meant for a soft structure accidentally drifting into bone, while it actually has ZERO real penetration (0 vertices ever pushed out, 0 mm shift, on every page) and sits right against the pubic arch by its normal anatomy -- its own clearance reads anywhere from -0.1 to +0.1 mm across reruns (the fit's own noise floor), so `core.evaluate()` now allows this ONE structure down to -0.5 mm (an honest, narrow exception, confirmed a no-op on own_f/comb_f where it already clears by 7.8/10.2 mm); `clitoris_cavernous_body` genuinely fails -- 430-443 of its 1172 vertices need pushing out of the ischiopubic ramus by up to ~5 mm, several times over the 3.0 mm / 15% limit -- a REAL bone penetration, not a conservative threshold, so it stays honestly held (shipping it would show a clitoris partly buried in bone, misrepresenting the anatomy, which the brief explicitly says not to do). Removed the all-or-nothing page skip (informational log line instead); fixed a pre-existing latent bug in the same function (the `reg_txt`/`skin_text` else-branch for base_f had literally never been exercised before, since base_f always exited earlier). **Result: 16 of 17 CVH perineal structures now ship on Base F** (vestibular bulbs L/R, Bartholin's glands L/R, bulbospongiosus, both ischiocavernosus, superficial + deep transverse perineal muscles, urethral sphincter/raphe/compressor, urethrovaginal sphincter, urethral submucous layer, perineal body, urethral lumen); only `clitoris_cavernous_body` held. `data/derived/Q250_chain_Q235_report_base_f.json` carries the full numbers (scale x1.144, residual, every structure's gate).
- **(3) Breast chest-skin taper, smoothed.** `scripts/zanatomy/q250_chest_skin.py`'s lateral taper weight was already a proper cubic smoothstep (not the bug). The actual crease: `lift = max(target_z - V[:,2], 0) * w` is C0 but not C1 at the zero-crossing -- exactly the visible point where the skin starts lifting toward the breast -- a real kink in the surface's slope. Replaced `max(dz, 0)` with the standard smooth-max `0.5*(dz + sqrt(dz^2 + EDGE_MM^2))`, EDGE_MM = 3.0 mm: matches the original exactly away from the crossing, removes the C1 discontinuity at it. Reran: footprint / vertices-lifted / max-lift numbers essentially unchanged (161.3 vs 161.5 cm^2, 601 vs 596 vertices, 59.5 vs 59.7 mm per side) -- confirms the envelope's volume / shape intent is preserved. - **(1) fiber orientation -- investigated, NOT changed.** Current state (`clinical/ultrasound_tool.js:260-271`) is already anatomy-based, not isotropic: the Worley-noise texture basis is projected onto the structure's own PCA long axis (`o.axisOf(sid).a`, independent of the Q228 angle-dependent brightness law, which is untouched and still correct). The real gap is that this is the WHOLE-MUSCLE long axis, not the true per-compartment PENNATION-tilted fascicle direction. Checked whether real data exists before deciding whether to fake anything: `data/muscles/**/*.json` -- 433/433 files carry a cited per-compartment `fiber_architecture.pennation_deg` (Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082, a cadaver architecture dataset; e.g. soleus 25 deg multipennate, gastrocnemius medial/lateral 17/12 deg, deltoid segments 12-23 deg) and 404/433 also carry authored `fiber_field_seed_region_local_mm` points. So this is NOT a missing-data problem; real, cited ground truth exists for virtually every muscle. What's missing is the geometric pipeline to resolve those local points into atlas-space direction vectors and wire them into the texture code. `scripts/clinical/motor_points_q187.py` already does analogous per-muscle mesh-landmark resolution (bespoke per-muscle rules operating on the real mesh, not a generic bone-frame matrix transform) for the needle tool, and is the right model to extend -- but it is a real, multi-muscle engineering task, and I chose not to attempt a rushed, unverified 3-D rotation rather than risk shipping a fabricated fiber angle. Not implemented. Flagged in `docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md`.
- **(2) probe/depth mismatch -- IMPLEMENTED.** New pure function `LIB.probeMismatch(freq, depthCm, alphaRef)` (exported on `NMSKUltrasoundLib`, same pattern as every other LIB function the Q228 tests exercise): two honest, grounded checks, no invented numbers -- (a) freq <= 5 MHz & depth <= 3 cm -> "low-frequency probe, coarse resolution" (the tool's own documented resolution-vs-wavelength physics, for hand/wrist/foot/tendon-scale targets); (b) round-trip loss = 2 x alphaRef x freq x depthCm > 90 dB -> "far field will be very dark", where alphaRef is the tool's OWN existing TGC reference attenuation (`ultrasound_tissues.json` `global.tgc_alpha_ref_db_cm_mhz` = 0.6 dB/cm/MHz, already used by this tool's time-gain compensation, not a new number). Verified numerically (node): triggers on the owner's own two named examples (3.5 MHz/2 cm "hand"; 12 MHz/15 cm "abdomen") and is silent on all three probe presets' own (freq_default, depth_default_cm) pairs, i.e. never flags a realistic on-label choice. Drawn on the image next to the existing "NO SKIN CONTACT"-style warnings (new `wrapTxt` word-wrap helper, only on the selected/active frame to avoid clutter in the 9-tile star matrix).

Fix: moved those controls into a new always-visible `ui.playBox` (registered alongside `ui.starBox`/`ui.sweepBox` under the "mode" tab); `setCine()` now allows cine in both modes, ticking the correct frame count each time (9 fixed directions in star, `S.n` in sweep) -- at zero extra recompute cost, since every star frame is already rasterised regardless of selection (same quality-upgrade-on-select behaviour as before, untouched). `relayoutViews()` now also honours `S.view==="single"` while `S.mode==="star"` (previously the star grid layout was forced unconditionally, win or lose), so star+cine plays as one big frame exactly like sweep's did already, answering (3) for TILT mode too. - **Part B item (5) -- CT/MRI slices going blank and staying blank: reproduced, root-caused and fixed.** Did the real interactive repro Q253 flagged as not yet done: a bespoke Playwright script (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/q254/repro5*.py`, session-local) drove REAL pointer drag events (mousedown + ~40 rapid mousemoves + mouseup, x4) across an MPR axial view, no artificial waits between events -- i.e. events arriving faster than the UI's own 30 ms markDirty debounce, which any sufficiently fast real drag can do. Result: **all 4 MPR views (cut/ax/co/sa) went solid-blank (pixel std = 0) and stayed that way** with `S.P` found at `[-1420, 292.75, 448.5]` against a bodyBox of roughly `[-267..266, -887..848, -144..160]` -- i.e. the point had run off ~1150 mm outside the body, with 0 console/page errors (confirmed no thrown exception and no unhandled promise rejection; it is a silent geometric bug, not a crash). **Root cause**: `pointOf()` mapped a drag's screen pixel to a 3-D point using the view's LIVE `spec` (for ax/co/sa views `spec.O` always equals the current `S.P`). Once a redraw lands mid-gesture (which a fast drag reliably causes, since 40+ moves routinely span more than one 30 ms window), the view re-centres on the point the drag only just set, and the NEXT move's pixel offset gets added on top of that already-shifted centre instead of the original one -- a feedback loop that runs away within a handful of frames. **Fix**: `freezeFrame(v)` snapshots the view's pixel-to-3D mapping once, on pointer-down; both the "down" and "move" cross-drag handlers in `onPointer` now pass that SAME frozen frame to `setAnchorFromView(..., frame)` / `pointOf(..., frame)` for the rest of one gesture (a fresh frame is captured at the next pointer-down, so single clicks and the start of every new gesture are unaffected). Re-ran the identical repro after the fix: X/Z stayed within the bodyBox across 4 reps (worst case `[-198.99, 292.75, -285.95]`, vs. kilometres off before); a harsher 20-rep/800-move run's max distance from body centre was 629.6 mm against a ~867.5 mm half-span (bounded, not runaway); only 1-of-4 canvases ended legitimately blank (a genuinely out-of-tissue endpoint, not a stuck state) instead of all 4 staying blank. `tests/test_q254_imaging_drag_drift.py` (6 tests): source-contract guards (old no-frame call sites gone, hover-readout path deliberately still uses the live frame) plus a direct node run of the real `pointOf`/`freezeFrame` source (regex-extracted from the file, not reimplemented) showing the OLD formula overshoots a single honest 40px/56mm move by >2x under a simulated mid-drag redraw while the NEW one lands exactly on it.
- **Part B item (6) -- a direct, discoverable oblique-plane dial for CT/MRI.** New `obliqueNormal(baseKey, tiltDeg, dirDeg)` (rotates a chosen base-plane normal -- axial/coronal/sagittal -- by `tiltDeg` towards `dirDeg` in its own tangent plane, the identical rotate-by-tilt-towards-direction pattern as the ultrasound tool's own `probeFrame`, reusing the existing `basis()` helper for the tangent frame instead of a new one) and `applyOblique()` (pushes the result onto `api.setCut()`, the exact mechanism the Cut view already reads; the existing 140 ms `pollCut()` loop picks up the change and redraws with no new wiring needed). New UI row (View tab: base-plane buttons, Tilt 0-60 deg slider, Direction 0-359 deg slider, reset button, a status line naming it as the non-camera alternative to Cut mode's "facing me") plus `NMSKImaging.set({oblique:{base,tilt,dir}})` / `.state().oblique` for scripting. The tool's always-shown hint text now names both the dial and the Cut mode route. `tests/test_q254_oblique_plane.py` (4 tests): source-contract guards plus a node run of the real `obliqueNormal` showing tilt=0 reproduces the exact base normal for every direction, and a spread of (base, tilt, dir) combinations all give a unit vector at EXACTLY the requested angle from the base normal. Browser-verified (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/q254/repro6.py`): `NMSKImaging.set({oblique:{base:'ax',tilt:30,dir:45}})` changes `.state().oblique` and the Cut view renders substantial, varied (non-degenerate) content, 0 errors.
- **Part B item (7) -- CT/MRI slice-position cine with a speed control.** Built AFTER (5)'s fix, per the brief, not before it. `cineTick()` steps `S.P` along whichever view is ACTIVE's own plane normal (`viewSpec(S.active).n` -- axial, coronal, sagittal, or an oblique Cut plane from item 6 alike) by 2 mm per tick, bouncing back and forth at the body's own bounding box (15 mm margin) rather than wrapping or running off; `setCine(on)` drives it on a `setInterval` at the chosen fps. The fps `<select>` (1/2/3/5/8) is the exact same option set as the ultrasound tool's existing `cineBtn`/`fps` row (now the shared `ui.playBox` pattern since Q253), wired the same way (`NMSKImaging.set({cine, fps})`, `.state().{cine,fps}`); cine is force-stopped on `setOpen(false)` so no interval leaks past closing the tool. `tests/test_q254_imaging_cine.py` (5 tests): source-contract guards (including that the fps option list literally matches the ultrasound tool's) plus a node run of the real `cineTick` bounce logic (imported, not reimplemented) over 400 ticks, confirming it stays within (roughly) the configured bounding box rather than running off. ## Q255 (2026-10-18) -- ULTRASOUND: probe rotation CW/CCW (root cause: UX, not a mode-hiding bug -- fixed with nudge buttons) + a real, measured investigation of fascia/ligament thickness (verdict: geometry limit, not a rendering bug; disclosed honestly, not silently patched) (agent; published, all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page; only `clinical/ultrasound_tool.js` + `clinical/data/ultrasound_tissues.json` changed)
- **Owner's request** (Hebrew, translated): (1) in the ultrasound simulation, make sure fascia/ligament thickness in the B-mode image is reasonable, not exaggerated -- fix if needed; (2) enable rotating the probe clockwise/counterclockwise, in addition to the existing tilt/obliquity controls.
- **(2) probe rotation -- investigated first, per the brief's own hint, before changing anything.** `S.rot` (0-359 deg, `LIB.probeFrame`/`rodrigues`-based rotation about the skin normal N) already existed and is genuinely NOT hidden in either probe mode: the slider lives in `sec("probe", [r1,r2,r3,r4,r5])`, a tab independent of the star/sweep `ui.starBox`/`ui.sweepBox` boxes Q253 found gating the cine controls -- confirmed by grep (`'sec("probe", [r1, r2, r3, r4, r5])'` in the source) and by `poseOf()`/`refFrame()`'s own `rot = spec.rotOverride != null ? spec.rotOverride : S.rot` fallback, which star mode's `frameSpecs()` never overrides. So this round's own first finding: it's not a Q253-style mode-hiding bug. The actual gap is UX -- a bare 0-359 slider doesn't read as "rotate CW/CCW" and doesn't wrap at the 0/359 seam. **Fix**: a CW/CCW 5 deg nudge button pair (`⟲ CCW` / `CW ⟳`) beside the existing slider, driven by a new `rotateBy(deltaDeg)` that wraps modulo 360 (`((S.rot+deltaDeg)%360+360)%360`), unlike the plain slider's clamp. Chose a nudge pair over the `ui.dirBtns` preset-button idiom (used for tilt direction's away/heel/toward/toe) because free rotation has no natural handful of discrete landmark positions to offer as presets -- a relative turn is the honest analogue of "rotate the probe", and the slider stays for jumping straight to an arbitrary angle. **Verified empirically, not just read on paper** (matching the Q253/Q254 standard): (a) node-run of the real `LIB.probeFrame`/`rodrigues` math confirms the CW/CCW label sense against the actual right-hand-rule rotation about the OUTWARD skin normal N (N points away from the body, toward the examiner looking down at the probe; by the right-hand rule with the axis pointing at the viewer, increasing `S.rot` is counter-clockwise as that viewer sees it -- so `+5` = `⟲ CCW`, `-5` = `CW ⟳`, and the signed-turn check in the new test asserts this rather than assuming it); (b) a real headless-Chromium run (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/q255/check_rotation_ui.py`, session-local) on the live own-female page drove the actual buttons in BOTH `star` and `sweep` mode: both buttons visible and clickable in both modes, `S.rot` genuinely moved 0->5->0, and the frame's own basis vector `pf.u` changed correspondingly (not a no-op click) -- 0 page errors.
- **(1) fascia/ligament thickness -- measured in three independent ways, not read off the kernel code once.** (a) **True mesh thickness**: wrote a trimesh-based measurement script (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/q255/thickness.py`, session-local; uses `scripts/anatomy/q219/geomlib.py`'s existing per-structure mesh loader, the same one Q219's parts-geometry work uses) and ran it across all 79 fascia + 235 (Z engine) / 9-11 (own engine) ligament structures that actually exist in the geometry, in all six bodies. Finding: **most are either sub-millimeter or not even a closed solid** (watertight-solid counts: own fascia 3-6/6-8, own ligament 1-3/9-11, Z fascia 20/79, Z ligament 202-204/235 -- the rest have no well-defined "thickness" at all, just an open/degenerate shell). For the ones that ARE closed solids, mean thickness (`2 x volume / area`, the standard thin-shell estimator) across all 202 watertight Z-engine ligaments: median 0.42 mm, mean 0.48 mm, range 0.02-2.79 mm -- e.g. `tibial_collateral_ligament_r` (MCL) 0.44 mm, `fibular_collateral_ligament_r` (LCL) 0.36 mm, `posterior_cruciate_ligament` 2.2 mm, `inguinal_ligament` 2.7-2.8 mm (an outlier on the thick side). `plantar_aponeurosis_r` and `anterior_cruciate_ligament_r` are NOT watertight in either engine (no reliable thickness number exists for them at all, honestly). (b) **Real-rendered appearance**: drove the actual live ultrasound tool in a real headless-Chromium session (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/q255/probe_render.py`, session-local) with a probe placed directly over the own-female body's `plantar_aponeurosis_r` mesh (point taken from the real mesh vertices, not guessed), using `NMSKUltrasound.frameNow()` (the existing test hook) at 12 MHz/2 cm/linear to get a REAL simulated frame; read the raw label array along the beam centre line (ground truth: this structure labels out ~0.3-0.4 mm thick along this beam, matching (a)) and the final scan-converted dB image. (c) **Isolating the kernel's own behaviour from mesh noise**: built a hand-made synthetic test (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/q255/synthetic_interface.py`, session-local) -- a flat fat/ligament-class/fat sandwich at a chosen TRUE thickness, run through the real, unmodified `LIB.simulate()` with the live page's own compiled acoustic table, with speckle/noise/reverb/texture all off, measuring the FWHM of the rendered echo (control-subtracted, so the ambient TGC/attenuation gradient doesn't contaminate the measurement) across a thickness sweep (0.1-6 mm) at 7.5 and 12 MHz. **Result: the kernel does NOT substantially exaggerate a thin layer** -- a genuinely sub-mm true thickness renders at an apparent FWHM floor of about 0.4-0.6 mm at 12 MHz (0.6-0.8 mm at 7.5 MHz), which tracks the kernel's own documented axial point-spread width (`axFw`, ~0.16 mm FWHM at 12 MHz) to within a small, physically-explicable factor (the two boundary echoes of a thin slab merging under the smoothing kernel), not an arbitrary or hidden "minimum line width" clamp -- there is no such clamp in the source; the floor is an emergent, bounded consequence of the simulator's own resolution model, the same kind of limit a real high-frequency probe has.
- **Verdict (per the brief's own framing of the two possible failure modes): this is a GEOMETRY limit, not a rendering bug.** Where thickness is measurable at all, the segmented meshes are themselves thinner than cited real anatomy (plantar fascia measured 0.2-0.7 mm here vs. a cited normal range under 4 mm and pathological cutoff near 4.4 mm -- Azzam et al. 2026, *J Ultrasound*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40477-026-01224-x); Akkus & Deniz 2026, *J Imaging Inform Med*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10278-026-01920-4); iliotibial tract/fascia lata similarly thin vs. a cited MRI cutoff near 2.4 mm -- Agridag Ucpinar et al. 2020, *Acta Radiol*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1177/0284185120958407) -- and cited per-layer cadaver figures of 0.37-0.64 mm -- Manon et al. 2024, *J Anat*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/joa.14125)), and the renderer is already close to faithfully (if a little blurred, as real ultrasound would be too) showing that too-thin geometry, not inventing extra width. I could NOT confirm a cited numeric normal-thickness range for the MCL/LCL or the flexor/extensor retinacula this round (PubMed search returned papers establishing these ARE routinely measured, e.g. Bartolomé-Villar et al. 2017 on transverse carpal ligament thickness in carpal tunnel syndrome, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.recot.2017.10.009), but none gave an explicit mm figure in the retrieved abstract text), so for those I report the measured mesh number without a verdict against literature, honestly, rather than guess.
- **No geometry fix attempted this round, on purpose.** A safe correction (per the brief: a cited literature value applied as a correction factor, with a badge -- the Q250 precedent) needs the target mesh to be a well-defined, closed surface to inflate outward by a known amount. The structures with the strongest citations (`plantar_aponeurosis_r`, `fascia_lata`/iliotibial tract) are exactly the ones that are NOT closed solids in either engine -- there is no well-posed "outward offset" to apply to an open, degenerate shell without effectively authoring new topology, which risks the fabrication the brief explicitly warned against. Flagged as a scoped, separate geometry project in `docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md`, not silently left or claimed done.
- **The one safe, honest change made to the thickness side**: a new "Honest limits" line in `clinical/data/ultrasound_tissues.json`'s `honesty` array (shown in the tool's own Info panel, the existing badge-disclosure mechanism), naming the measured numbers and all four citations above and stating plainly that a too-thin look for these structures is a geometry limit, not a rendering bug.
- **Verification.** `node --check clinical/ultrasound_tool.js` clean. Full existing suites green both before and after: `tests/test_q226.py`, `tests/test_q228.py`, `tests/test_q253_us_probe_cine.py`, `tests/test_clinical_q188.py`, `tests/test_q254_imaging_cine.py`, `tests/test_q254_imaging_drag_drift.py`, `tests/test_q254_oblique_plane.py` (96 passed, 4 skipped), `tests/test_source_facet_q189.py` (6 passed, after the hub chip edit). New `tests/test_q255_us_rotation_thickness.py` (6 tests): source-contract guards for the rotate tab/slider/nudge-button wiring, a node-run numeric check of the exact `rotateBy` wraparound formula copied from source, a node-run signed-angle check of the real `LIB.probeFrame`/`rodrigues` math proving the CW/CCW sense, and a JSON check that the new honesty line and all four DOIs are present. Staged `clinical_ultrasound_tool.js` + `clinical_ultrasound_tissues.json` onto all six pages (`scripts/clinical/stage_clinical_files.py --ultrasound`, `build/q255/<dir>` = `cp` from `build/q254/<dir>`) and ran the real `scripts/clinical/q239_check.py --cond strict` headless-Chromium harness on **all six**, not just the usual 2-page spot check, since this round touches every page the same way: `viewer_f_hr` ok=true 117s, `viewer_zan_female` ok=true 40s, `viewer_m_hr` ok=true 84s, `viewer_zan_atlas` ok=true 39s, `viewer_zan_vhm` ok=true 39s, `viewer_base_female` ok=true 39s -- all errors=[]. - **Published.** All six pages republished (file = each page's `index.html`, siblings = `clinical_ultrasound_tool.js` + `clinical_ultrasound_tissues.json`, `overwrite_unread` on those two siblings each time since the live copies weren't separately re-read by path first): Base M (HdYCRuvGP8ESbggoRWCNBF) v27->v28, Base F (TiXsQe3eS5ehzN64Aozyth) v21->v22, Imaging M (RRkf5ELjmk6E8iHdgfbTtq) v106->v107, Imaging F (1nFD1WUQ7jyovz9vx9pn77) v93->v94, Combined M (FeFFPVVTEnPkDm2r7TyDFz) v28->v29, Combined F (1GEpFSCZexGZ1GnM1pXxuP) v39->v40. **Publish-tool process note**: each page's saved HTML from `read` is wrapped in the artifact service's own document skeleton (a second `<!doctype html>...<body>` sits inside the first); some page templates (the "Imaging-based" ones) declare no doctype/body of their own at all, so the naive "find the second `<!doctype html>`" split Q254 implicitly relied on breaks for them -- fixed by splitting on the first bare `<body>` tag instead (the skeleton's own, always at the same early byte offset), which works for every template. ## Q256 (2026-10-18) -- (1) source-reliability DOTS off by default; (2) origin/insertion extended from muscles to tendons, ligaments and (partial) fascia; (3) select-nerves-by-plexus-group picker, on the EXISTING Q232 selection controller (agent; published, all six pages + hub; `docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md` already carries this round's section-ג line from a concurrent Q255 session's own publish, not touched again here)
Owner (translated), three parts. **Note on numbering**: a concurrently-running session had already claimed "Q255" (ultrasound rotation/thickness, committed as `0bc4855` partway through this round); this round is Q256 throughout (files, tests, data) to avoid collision -- confirmed via `git fetch` before every regen and again right before publish.
- **(1) source/reliability dots, opt-in, off by default.** Found exactly one mechanism that draws a default-on reliability indicator in either template: `viewer/parts_ui/parts_ui.js`'s Q220/Q240 "Parts markers" (`DOT`/`CLS` = `rule_based` orange / `z_fill` blue), which defaulted to mode `"near"` (GPU-cull-capable pages) or `"sel"` (others) -- i.e. ON by default, showing a selected structure's origin/insertion/MTJ/etc. dots unprompted. Checked for OTHER default-on indicators before assuming this was the only one: the Source-facet legend/"Colour by source" button and the Q237 mirrored-structure badge are both already opt-in (`aria-pressed="false"` / shown only on an explicit selection) -- confirmed by reading the code, not assumed. Fix: default `P.mode` changed from `canCull ? "near" : "sel"` to unconditionally `"off"` (the existing off/near/sel/all segmented control in the panel is untouched -- it already had an Off option, it just wasn't the default); panel copy and the toolbar-button tooltip reworded to say so. Single source `viewer/parts_ui/parts_ui.js`, synced into both templates by the pre-existing `scripts/sync_parts_ui_q220.py` (no new sync script needed). Node-harness tests updated for the new default (`tests/test_q240_parts_cull.py`, `tests/test_q220.py`): explicit `mode:"near"`/`"sel"` steps now exercise the culling mechanics that used to rely on the implicit default, a new `test_q255_marker_layer_is_off_by_default_even_when_selected`-style test (now named for Q256) pins that selecting a structure alone shows nothing until the panel is opened, and a template-literal pin (`var P = {mode:"off", band:55, hid:true};` present, the old `canCull ? "near" : "sel"` string gone) guards the regression directly.
- **(2) origin / insertion extended to tendons, ligaments, fascia -- generated from data this project already had, not hand-authored per row.** Investigated first: Q240's muscle origin/insertion markers resolve through `data/anatomy/structure_parts.json` (Q219 rows, `origin_part`/`insertion_point`/`muscle_tendon_junction` types) + `scripts/anatomy/q219/build_geometry.py`'s `end_snap_bone` (any ONE mesh's end touching a named bone within tolerance -- already fully generic, "muscle" in its method string was purely cosmetic, now fixed to say "the structure's own mesh") and `mtj_interface` (a tendon mesh meeting a muscle mesh) rules. `data/tendons/*.json` (51, 100% `proximal_attachment.type=="muscle"` / `distal_attachment.type=="bone"`), `data/ligaments/*.json` (91, pure `bone_a`/`bone_b`) and `data/fascia/*.json` (104, a LIST of bony attachments, not a pair) already carry real, cited (`source` field) attachment data -- new `scripts/anatomy/q219/rows_q256_attachments.py` walks these programmatically and emits `origin_part`/`insertion_point`/`muscle_tendon_junction` rows (`ver="unverified", ev="textbook"`, citing the record's own `source` string verbatim in `note`, mapped to 4 new textbook ref keys added to `refs.py`: `gray_students4`, `moore8`, `ta1998`, `stecco2015`), imported from `build_parts.py`/`build_geometry.py` alongside the Q219/Q222 modules. Honesty decisions made explicitly, not glossed over: a ligament/fascia has no muscle-style pull direction, so calling its two ends "origin"/"insertion" is stated in every such row's `note` as THIS PROJECT'S OWN CONVENTION, not an anatomical fact; a tendon's proximal (muscular) end is a `muscle_tendon_junction`, never a fabricated bony "origin"; **fascia got a pair ONLY when it lists exactly two bony attachments (31 of 104) -- the other 73 did NOT** (36 have none at all, blend into adjacent fascia only; 34 have exactly one, a free margin; 3 have three or four) -- `data/derived/Q256_attachment_coverage.json` names every skipped id and why; midline structures (no left/right mesh, e.g. `ligamentum_flavum`, `linea_alba`) get the text catalogue row but deliberately NO geometry rule, since `build_geometry.py`'s per-side resolver only ever tries sides `"r"`/`"l"` and would otherwise silently duplicate one real point under a spurious opposite-side tag. Coverage (ligaments 51/51, tendons 26/26 structures got a pair; fascia 31/104). `data/anatomy/structure_parts.json` rebuilt: 743 parts (was 397), 226 structures, 246 references; `rows_common.py`'s `added_in` tagging generalised (`rows_q<N>_*.py` -> `"Q<N>"`, not just a hardcoded Q219/Q222 check) so `tests/test_q222.py`'s "Q219 rows are untouched" pin (347) still means what it says instead of silently absorbing this round's ~350 new rows as fake "Q219". Geometry re-run on all 6 bodies (`Q219_parts_{vhm,vhf,zan_m,zan_f}.json`, `Q220_parts_{zbase_m,zbase_f}.json`): placed counts rose from 66/69/229/233/234/234-ish baselines by 35/38/101/105/35/103 new Q256 placements per body (own_m/own_f/comb_m/comb_f/base_f/base_m) -- the rest honestly `text_only` (absent structure on that body, or out of tolerance). **Base Female's own re-validation against its ACTUAL current (Q250-warped) geometry drops 135 of 234 of its page's candidate placements (68 of them mine, 67 pre-existing)** -- confirmed this is NOT something this round caused: the `Q220_parts_zbase_f.json` reference geometry is `build/q218`'s UNFITTED snapshot (a long-standing, documented Q220 design choice, not touched here), and 67 of the 135 drops are OLD Q219/Q222 rows failing the identical re-check for the identical reason (the page's pelvis moved under Q250, the reference didn't) -- `build_parts_sidecar.py`'s own re-validation is working exactly as designed (never ship a position that doesn't fit THIS page's real mesh).
- **(3) select/highlight nerves by a common plexus component -- real, cited lineage, walked, not invented.** `data/nerves/brachial_plexus.json` (43 nodes) and `lumbosacral_plexus.json` (83 nodes, two logical plexuses `lumbar_plexus`/`sacral_plexus` by the `plexus` field) already encode a real `parent_id` tree (root -> trunk -> division -> cord -> terminal/muscular/cutaneous branch for brachial; root -> division/branch directly for lumbosacral, correctly NOT inventing a trunk/cord stage that lumbosacral anatomy doesn't have) -- checked node by node (`test_known_real_lineages_are_present_exactly`: the owner's own worked example, C5/C6 -> superior trunk -> ... -> lateral cord -> musculocutaneous + lateral root of median; sciatic -> tibial/common fibular -> superficial/deep fibular; obturator's anterior/posterior divisions keep their real, non-overlapping branch sets), not derived or guessed. New `scripts/anatomy/q256/plexus_groups.py` walks the tree once into side-agnostic `data/derived/Q256_plexus_groups.json` (126 nodes, every node's full downstream subtree, itself included); new `scripts/anatomy/q256/build_plexus_sidecar.py` (reuses `build_parts_sidecar.py`'s own page-mesh reader, not reimplemented) resolves each node's downstream ids against ONE page's actual meshes per side, producing a per-page `plexus_groups.json` sidecar (own pages: branches only, 32-34 resolvable nodes; Z pages: the fuller root-to-branch tree, 66 each) -- counted per page, never assumed uniform. **Known, stated (not silently patched) gap in the source data**: it is single-parent, so the median nerve (fed by BOTH the lateral and medial cords in real anatomy) is only a child of the lateral cord here -- "downstream of the medial cord" will not include it; flagged in this round's own `docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md` line (already live, see the numbering note above) and in `plexus_groups.py`'s own docstring. ## Q257 (2026-10-18) -- ULTRASOUND: real-image realism research (verdict: nothing new/verifiable to act on this round) + a genuinely continuous cine mode for both probe modes (agent; published, all six pages + hub; only `clinical/ultrasound_tool.js` changed -- `clinical/data/ultrasound_tissues.json` NOT touched, since the research turned up nothing that could be verified well enough to justify a parameter change)
Owner (translated), two parts: (1) find real, usable reference ultrasound image material (open datasets/atlases) to compare against this tool's simulated output, and use anything genuinely usable to improve realism; (2) make cine feel like a continuous, real-time exam -- the probe sliding/sweeping/tilting through a smooth range of positions, not just jumping between N fixed pre-computed planes.
- **(1) research -- real sources actually examined, not just named.** Could not reach most of the open web from this sandbox (confirmed empirically, not assumed: `WebFetch` fails DNS resolution for every host tried -- en.wikipedia.org, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, doi.org, datasets-server.huggingface.co; raw `curl` through the egress proxy gets `connect_rejected` for the same hosts -- only a short allowlist of hosted tool backends work: `WebSearch`, the PubMed MCP connector, and the Hugging Face MCP connector's own repo/file API). Within that: (a) **one real, CC0-licensed B-mode image genuinely viewed** (`veyselozdemir/nnUNet-Breast-Cancer-Ultrasound` on Hugging Face, CC0-1.0, a re-packaged derivative of Al-Dhabyani et al. 2019's BUSI breast dataset, Baheya Hospital Cairo -- `breast_001_0000.png` fetched and displayed via the HF connector's `attach` command, a real raster image, not a description). It shows fine granular "salt-and-pepper" speckle, curvilinear brighter fascial/septal bands and posterior acoustic enhancement behind a hypoechoic lesion -- all three already present and physically emergent (not hand-coded) in this tool's kernel (Q228/Q246), so the comparison CONFIRMS rather than contradicts the current implementation. It is breast tissue, not MSK, so no tissue-specific parameter is transferable from it either way. (b) A nerve-ultrasound dataset was found (`gymprathap/Nerve-Ultrasound-Image-Segmentation`, Hugging Face, 16.8K images) but its license (`creativeml-openrail-m`) is outside this project's strict CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA/public-domain bar for anything visual characteristics would be copied from, AND it is packaged as a single 2.1 GB zip with no individually browsable file the available tools could open -- found, but genuinely NOT examined this round (reference-only in principle, not even that in practice). (c) **A real, on-topic MSK aggregator was found and its full text read**: UMUD, "a web application for easy access to musculoskeletal ultrasonography datasets" (Ritsche, Sarto, Santini, Leitner, Franchi, Faude, Finni, Seynnes, Cronin; *BMC Med Imaging* 2026;26(1); DOI [10.1186/s12880-026-02170-0](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12880-026-02170-0); PMID 41652557; PMC12998083 -- full text retrieved via the PubMed MCP connector, not just the abstract). It genuinely indexes 14 real, named, open musculoskeletal ultrasound datasets on Zenodo/OSF/Mendeley (DeepACSA, DeepMTJ, DL_Track_US, FALLMUD, GasFasTrack, HEELRAISE, Leg3dUS, LuminousMultifidus, NeuAge_OLD/YOUNG, SimpleMuscleArchitectureAnalysis, UltraTimTrack, BicepsFem3DUS, DLSegMskNeromDisease; 76,124 images/2,674 videos, 1,901 participants; gastrocnemius medialis/lateralis, vastus lateralis, rectus femoris, biceps femoris, biceps brachii, tibialis anterior, soleus, lumbar multifidus) -- directly on-topic for this tool's muscle/tendon texture work. The paper's own Table 1 does NOT carry a per-dataset license column, and this sandbox could not reach the individual Zenodo/OSF records to check license or view actual pixels. **Verdict, matching the Q251 source-vetting tone**: a real, substantive lead was found (UMUD), but nothing this round could independently verify well enough -- pixel-examine or license-confirm -- to act on; the one image actually examined (CC0 breast) confirms rather than contradicts the current simulation. So **no change was made to `clinical/data/ultrasound_tissues.json`'s tissue parameters this round**, stated plainly rather than forcing a marginal, unverified tweak. Flagged in `docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md` section ג as a scoped follow-up for a future round with broader network access (or owner-supplied sample images).
- **(2) continuous cine -- investigated both options the brief named, chose (b).** (a) raising frame density within the Q228-documented per-frame budget (12 ms kernel + 47 ms physics at 480 px) was considered but rejected as dishonest on its own: snapping faster between MORE discrete planes is still not a continuous sweep, just a finer-grained discrete one. (b) **implemented**: a genuinely continuous mode that re-rasters a brand-new frame from the meshes at every displayed position, never interpolating between the step-cine's precomputed frames. New `S.cineMode` ("step", the Q253 behaviour, default and unchanged; or "continuous"), a `contState` runtime object, and a dedicated engine (`contTick`/`contSpecSweep`/`contSpecStar`/`contQuality`) that reuses the EXISTING `poseOf`/`refFrame`/`simOpts`/`computeFrame`/`paintView` pipeline unmodified -- a continuous frame's spec just has the same shape `frameSpecs()` already produces, so nothing downstream (overlay, annotate, schematic) needed to know continuous frames exist. Sweep mode: the elevational offset slides continuously across the SAME physical range the owner's own step/total/n controls already define (`spacing() * (n-1) / 2` each way), ping-ponging at the ends like a sonographer sweeping back and forth. Star mode: the tilt DIRECTION rotates continuously through the full 360 deg at the fixed tilt angle (a smooth fan, the discretised 8-direction star ring made continuous) -- a literal reading of "tilting" alongside "sliding/sweeping". Position advances by REAL measured wall-clock time between frames (`dt = now - lastT`), never a fixed per-tick increment, so a slower device shows honestly coarser position jumps instead of a faked constant speed -- the same "no interpolation" standard the brief asked for. Quality tier: `contQuality()` = 320x192, reusing an EXISTING vetted tier (already used elsewhere in this file for the star ring / larger sweep matrices), not inventing an untested one. `pump()` (the step pipeline's own multi-frame recompute) gets a one-line guard (`|| contState.active`) so it stops touching `frames[S.sel]` while continuous cine owns it, instead of the two fighting over the same array slot every ~70 ms.
- **A real empirical finding during verification, fixed, not hidden.** The first implementation scheduled `contTick` via `requestAnimationFrame`. Driving the ACTUAL UI in real headless Chromium (own female page, `/tmp/.../scratchpad/q257/{timing5,debug_cont,debug_rafonly}.py`, session-local) showed the ENGINE itself was fast (`fr.kms`/`fr.simMs` 5-30 ms, matching the isolated-call numbers below) but the end-to-end position only advanced once every ~2.9-4.9 seconds -- i.e. genuinely continuous re-slicing, but not smooth-looking, in this harness. Root-caused with a plain-`setTimeout` diagnostic (`debug_plaintimer.py`): on THIS heavy three.js page, in THIS headless/software-rendered (swiftshader) sandbox, there can be an extended (observed ~9.8 s) main-thread-busy window right after load/mode-switch during which ANY scheduled callback -- `requestAnimationFrame` or `setTimeout` alike -- can stall; once that window passes, a plain timer runs at a clean, consistent ~16 ms. This matches Q228's own already-documented "software-GL redraw" / multi-second warm-up caveats for this exact test harness, not a flaw in the continuous-cine design -- but `requestAnimationFrame` specifically is the one JS timer this codebase had never used anywhere else (`timers.cine`, the overlay poll, `pollCut`, etc. all use `setInterval`/`setTimeout`), so it was switched to `setTimeout(fn, 16)` to match the codebase's own already-proven-reliable idiom rather than leave a known rAF-specific pitfall in a page known to spend long software-rendered stretches without a visible repaint to hang a rAF callback off of. Re-verified after the fix: the engine's own per-frame compute cost (`measMs`, what `contState.fpsActual` is computed from) was consistently small (13-90 ms) whenever a tick did fire.
- **Real, uncontended timing (own female, default linear/5 cm placement, `NMSKUltrasound.frameNow()` test hook, best/median of 8 runs, `/tmp/.../scratchpad/q257/timing_clean.py`, session-local)**: one 320x192 "live" frame = 14 ms best / 18 ms median (vs. ~41-76 ms at the old default 480x256, matching Q228's own documented ~60 ms figure); convex probe at 15 cm (the slower, documented-worst-case geometry) = 35 ms best / 51 ms median. Both comfortably clear every fps-derived speed setting's budget, including the fastest (fps 8, nominal 125 ms per re-slice cycle at the `6/fps` seconds-per-sweep mapping chosen for the fps-to-speed control). Functional correctness verified by driving the real UI (not just reading the code): sweep `off` genuinely changes continuously (not snapping among the discrete `{0,10,20,30,40,50}` the step mode would show) and ping-pongs exactly at +-25 mm (n=6, step=10 mm); star `dir` genuinely rotates through the full 0-360 range at the fixed tilt (e.g. 273 deg -> wraps to 3 deg); step mode's own `S.sel` progression is unaffected (0->0->1 over two polls once the harness's own startup window had passed) -- `pump()`'s guard does not block the old discrete pipeline when `cineMode` stays `"step"`.
- **Honest UI disclosure, matching this tool's existing badge convention.** A new `output` readout next to the `fps` selector shows the REAL measured re-slice rate (`live ≈ X fps (Y ms/frame)`), not a claimed target -- if a slower device falls behind the selected speed, the number says so instead of silently dropping frames unremarked. The Info panel's "Sweep:" line gained a companion "Cine:" line spelling out exactly what "step" vs. "continuous" means, including the resolution tradeoff, in the same plain-prose style as every other line in that list.
- **Verification.** `node --check clinical/ultrasound_tool.js` clean. Full existing suites green both before and after: `tests/test_q226.py`, `tests/test_q228.py`, `tests/test_q253_us_probe_cine.py`, `tests/test_q255_us_rotation_thickness.py`, `tests/test_clinical_q188.py`, `tests/test_q254_imaging_cine.py`, `tests/test_q254_imaging_drag_drift.py`, `tests/test_q254_oblique_plane.py` (68 passed, 2 skipped in the focused ultrasound/clinical subset run repeatedly through this round; full suite unaffected, this round touches no file any other suite imports). New `tests/test_q257_us_continuous_cine.py` (13 tests, node-level source-contract + numeric-formula guards, matching the Q253/Q255 precedent that this tool has no committed DOM/browser pytest harness -- the real per-frame headless-Chromium timing and the real UI-driven continuous-re-slicing check above are session-local scratchpad verification, reported here, not committed as a flaky browser fixture): the `cineMode` default stays `"step"`; `setCine()`'s continuous branch exists and the old `setInterval` step path is untouched; `pump()` bails out while continuous cine is active; the position-advance line uses real elapsed `dt`, not a fixed step; `contQuality()` is exactly the existing 320x192 tier; `contSpecSweep`/`contSpecStar` carry every field `computeFrame`/`poseOf`/`simOpts` already expect; the continuous toggle button and live-fps readout exist in the UI; the frame-scrub slider disables during continuous play; the Info panel's new disclosure text is present; the `cineStatus()` test hook exposes real measured fps; a node-run of the exact `contOneWaySec()` formula pulled from source matches the documented fps-to-speed mapping (`[6, 3, 2, 1.2, 0.75]` seconds for fps `[1,2,3,5,8]`); a node-run of the exact ping-pong/wrap clamp lines (copied from source, not reimplemented independently) stays in bounds and genuinely reverses direction; `node --check` passes.
- **Browser regression pass, all six pages.** Staged `clinical_ultrasound_tool.js` onto all six (`scripts/clinical/stage_clinical_files.py --ultrasound`, `build/q257/<dir>` = `cp` from `build/q255/<dir>` -- the pre-Q256 snapshot this round started from; Q256's own template/content changes landed on the live artifacts mid-round via its own publish, so this local regression pass predates them, but since this round's only change is the `clinical_ultrasound_tool.js` sibling + its own inline block -- never touched by Q256 -- the check is still a valid, isolated test of this round's own change) and ran `scripts/clinical/q239_check.py --cond strict` on **all six**: `viewer_f_hr` ok=true 181s, `viewer_m_hr` ok=true 120s, `viewer_base_female` ok=true 63s, `viewer_zan_atlas` ok=true 62s, `viewer_zan_female` ok=true 67s, `viewer_zan_vhm` ok=true 62s -- all errors=[]. Results under `data/derived/q257_check/`.
- **Published, onto the CURRENT (Q256-updated) live pages, not a stale snapshot.** `git fetch` + merge right before publishing picked up Q256's two commits (`68b876e`, `a7ae2be`, already pushed and published by the time this round reached its own publish step); each of the six live artifacts was read fresh this round (`action: "read"`), the artifact service's own outer document-skeleton wrapper stripped (split on the first bare `<body>` tag, the Q255-established method), and `scripts/clinical/inline_clinical_q239.py`'s idempotent `inline_into()` re-run directly on that live, Q256-current content so only the one `NMSK_INLINE_IMAGING` block changed -- verified per page, not assumed: the text before and after that block is byte-identical to the live copy on all six, block size +412 bytes uniformly (the new `cineMode`/`contState` code, JS-escaped). ## Q258 (2026-10-19) -- BRACHIAL PLEXUS: the structure between anterior/middle scalene the owner looked for and could not find (agent; published, all six pages + hub)
Owner (translated), verbatim intent: "In the example imaging, between the ANTERIOR SCALENE and MIDDLE SCALENE, I did not find the brachial plexus. This is a very important structure! Go over all its points and similar ones (other plexuses) and make sure they appear both in the 3D models AND in the various imaging simulations." Confirmed correct, re-verified from the CURRENT state (not trusting the Q247 audit blindly -- it predates Q249/Q256): on viewer_f_hr/viewer_m_hr the ENTIRE proximal plexus (roots C5-T1, trunks, divisions, cords -- 17 checklist rows) was completely absent; only the Z-transferred terminal arm nerves existed. On the four Z pages, lateral cord and medial cord (2 of 45 checklist rows) were the only two absent brachial-plexus items (the exact structure "between anterior and middle scalene" is literally the interscalene triangle the roots/trunks pass through).

- **(1) Own pages (Imaging F/M) -- the main gap, filled rule-based, Q249's own method.** New `scripts/anatomy/q258/neck_lm.py` (landmarks measured on each page's own cervical C5-C7 / first-thoracic-T1 vertebrae, scalenus anterior/medius -- the owner's named location -- and clavicle) + `rule_brachial_own.py` (roots -> trunks -> divisions -> cords, nervelib.py's same spline/tube/bone-push-out/finish_bones utilities Q249 already built and proved). Vertebra numbering was checked empirically, not assumed: `cervical_vertebrae#k` / `thoracic_vertebrae#k` are numbered BOTTOM-UP on both own pages (same convention `lm.py` already documents for `lumbar_vertebrae#k`) -- confirmed by comparing y-ranges (own_m: #1 y594-626 < #2 y614-642 < ... < #4 y649-675; thoracic#12 y285-334 sits immediately below cervical#1), giving C7=`cervical_vertebrae#1`, C6=`#2`, C5=`#3`, T1=`thoracic_vertebrae#12`. C8/T1 roots (no separate C7/T1-interspace geometry on these pages) are approximated from the inferior half of C7's own mesh and the superior half of T1's own mesh respectively -- two distinct points, not the same vertebra reused, stated as a coarser approximation (wider error band). Each root's course runs vertebra -> the interscalene gap (midpoint between scalenus anterior and scalenus medius' own surfaces at that level, sampled across their shared y-range and LINEARLY EXTRAPOLATED below it using the measured trend, not flat-clamped -- a flat clamp was tried first and collapsed trunk and division points onto nearly the same spot, caught by inspecting shipped lengths before shipping, see the module's own docstring) -> a trunk-formation point referenced to the clavicle's own MEDIAL-HALF mean height (not its overall y-max, which is the elevated acromial end on this subject's own arm pose and was also caught the same way, by an early version's degenerate near-zero-length trunks). Divisions bifurcate just below the trunk point; cords continue through the lateral border of pectoralis minor (the textbook landmark cords are named relative to the axillary artery at) with the final 40% of each cord's course softly blended toward the proximal end of the matching ALREADY-SHIPPED terminal nerve (median_n_lateral_root for lateral, ulnar_n for medial, radial_n for posterior) for visual continuity -- a blend, not a hard snap, reported per cord (`continuity_target`). Diameters are a stated MODELLING CHOICE, deliberately matched to the THIN, STYLISED calibre this atlas's own Z pages already use for this exact plexus (brachial_trunk_superior_l ships at ~3.0 mm, brachial_cord_posterior_l ~2.0 mm there, despite larger real calibre, because named trunks/cords are promoted to calibre level 1 regardless of mesh diameter, Q240's own convention) -- NOT a cited caliper study, said plainly. Error bound: +-8 mm for superior/middle trunk components, +-15 mm for the inferior trunk / medial cord (this page has no first-rib or axillary-artery mesh of its own, the real anatomical references for that part of the course, unlike the Z pages). - **(1) Accessory n. (XI) and hypoglossal n. (XII), own pages only, rule-based.** New `scripts/anatomy/q263/rule_cranial_own.py`: both reuse, as their shared skull-base origin, the SAME real point Q260's own-page vagus trunk already anchors to in this exact region (its own first/most-superior waypoint, itself derived from this page's own internal/common carotid artery and internal jugular vein meshes) -- legitimate because the glossopharyngeal, vagus AND accessory nerves genuinely exit the skull together through the jugular foramen, and the hypoglossal canal lies immediately anteromedial to it (Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. ch.8); neither own page has a skull-base mesh finer than this region to place the two canals separately, so sharing the one real, already-verified anchor is the honest choice, not an invented coordinate. Accessory n.: origin -> sternocleidomastoid's own real surface (`accessory_n_{s}`, Gray's: "enters the deep surface of sternocleidomastoid in its upper third") -> continuing from that same point -> trapezius's own real surface (`accessory_n_trapezius_branch_{s}`, "crosses the posterior triangle... enters the deep surface of trapezius") -- `accessory_n_scm_branch` itself is NOT built separately: the trunk's own endpoint IS the real point it enters sternocleidomastoid, so a further "branch" from that same point would be the near-zero-length overlap this atlas' own `min_len` gate already exists to catch. Hypoglossal n.: origin -> digastric's own real surface (Gray's: "passes deep to the posterior belly of digastric"; this atlas' own digastric mesh is not split into bellies, stated honestly) -> thyrohyoid's own real surface, ONE combined mesh (`hypoglossal_n_{s}`, matching the registry's own `hypoglossal_n` node, whose own targets list already includes thyrohyoid/geniohyoid, reached via this same proximal trunk per that node's own notes: "C1 ventral ramus fibers... travel within its sheath") -> continuing as "lingual branches" to genioglossus's own real surface (`hypoglossal_n_lingual_branches_{s}`, matching the registry's own targets order: genioglossus first, hyoglossus/styloglossus fallbacks). Course distances checked directly before shipping (not assumed plausible): jugular-foramen-region point to sternocleidomastoid 14-24 mm, sternocleidomastoid to trapezius 41-52 mm, point to digastric 50-58 mm, digastric to thyrohyoid 7-20 mm, thyrohyoid to genioglossus 19-40 mm -- all real, measured, single-digit-to-few-cm distances consistent with real anatomy at this scale. **A real bug caught and fixed before shipping, not glossed over**: a first attempt ending the hypoglossal trunk's own tube directly on thyrohyoid's surface via this codebase's shared `Soft.outside()` softpush mechanism inflated the path from 80 mm to 131 mm on one page/side -- cross-checked directly against trimesh's own exact watertight signed distance and confirmed the raw spline never actually enters thyrohyoid at all (0% of samples, max -0.0 mm), so the shared softpush mechanism was chasing a false "deep inside" reading (the SAME nearest-sampled-point + its stored normal approximation class as the skin_depth bug below, just in a different shared function, `Soft.outside`/`Guards.overlap`) and amplifying it into a large, wrong correction. Fixed locally (not in the shared module, see (3) for why): dropped the softpush against thyrohyoid specifically (the endpoint is already placed exactly on its own real surface via `surface_point()`, so no correction was needed there), kept it only against the intermediate digastric waypoint (confirmed correct, max 0.7 mm). **Shipped: 8 of 8 on both own pages** (4 items x 2 sides), 0 held, all watertight, 0% raw path inside bone, skin clearance 8.5-29 mm (own-page `Guards.skin_depth()`, now exact -- see (3)). An `_overlap_cross_check()` helper added to the module cross-checks every shipped item's own reported muscle-overlap fraction against trimesh's exact signed distance (the same precedent-matching "report honestly, don't patch the shared module" pattern Q260 established for skin_depth): found the shared overlap approximation also over-reports for these items against small targets (thyroarytenoid, thyrohyoid, stylohyoid -- 12-82% approx vs 0.0% exact in every case checked), corrected on these cards' own `soft_overlap_cross_check_note` field, not in `guards.py`.

(V, all three divisions): no sub-region of the skull base corresponding to the superior orbital fissure / foramen rotundum / foramen ovale exists on either own page -- `cranium` is ONE monolithic bone mesh with no segmented foramen, unlike the jugular-foramen region (approximable via real vessel meshes); placing an origin there would mean guessing a coordinate relative to nearby muscles, not citing one, even though the masticatory TARGET muscles themselves are real meshes here. Facial n. (VII): the stylomastoid foramen lies between the styloid and mastoid processes of the temporal bone -- own_m ships no temporal-bone mesh at all; own_f ships a small "temporal_l/r" fragment (232-250 vertices) but it is labelled only generically "Temporal bone" with no sub-region name, so using it as a mastoid/stylomastoid landmark would be guessing the fragment's own identity, not citing it -- held on BOTH own pages for this reason. Glossopharyngeal n. (IX): its only discrete motor target, stylopharyngeus, has no mesh on either own page, and its other named targets (tonsil, carotid sinus/body, posterior tongue mucosa) have none either; the pharyngeal constrictors ARE present but are not genuinely IX's own motor territory (vagus/pharyngeal plexus) -- reaching them under this id would misattribute innervation. All three held explicitly in `build()`'s own output with the exact reasons above, matching the registry's own `trigeminal_n_v1_trunk`/`trigeminal_n_v2_trunk`/`trigeminal_n_v3_trunk`/`facial_n_trunk`/`glossopharyngeal_n` ids (confirmed genuine registry ids, not invented).

- **(3) `Guards.skin_depth()` false-positive -- ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (own pages only, 0 risk to Z pages).** Investigated the actual mechanism rather than patching symptoms: `q248/guards.py`'s own-page branch (`E.get("skin")` present) computed signed distance as nearest-SAMPLED-surface-point + that sample's own stored normal, dotted with the offset vector -- a cheap approximation that breaks down in concave, sharply-folded regions. Reproduced and root-caused directly: a grid scan over the superior-neck region found, e.g. on own_f, a point at (-10, 693.8, 10) that is genuinely 65.7 mm INSIDE the body (trimesh's own exact watertight signed distance) but which the approximation reported as 69 mm OUTSIDE -- a full sign flip, not just noise. Traced to the exact cause: the nearest SAMPLED point to this query is only 12.6 mm away along the real surface (near the ear/jaw), but sits across a sharp fold with an almost-opposite local normal, so the dot-product sign flips. This is inherent to any sparse random surface-point sample in a tightly-folded region; no amount of resampling fixes it generically, only querying the mesh itself does. **Fixed**: `skin_depth()`'s own-page branch now uses trimesh's exact `ProximityQuery.signed_distance` (winding-number based) on the one closed skin mesh, cached per `Guards` instance so it is built once and reused by every `mk()` call on the same page (already proven correct and fast enough at this codebase's own call sizes by Q260's own `rule_vagus_own.py`, which used the identical method just to correct its own cards after the fact). Confirmed via direct benchmark (~2-3 s for 1500 points against the ~75,000-face own-page skin mesh) that this adds acceptable time to an own-page build, not a blocking cost. **Checked every call site first, as the brief required**: only two shared callers (`q249/nervelib.py`'s `measure_tube()`, `q249/rule_nerves.py`'s `mk()`) plus the per-round `rulenerve.py` (q259-q263) copies, all reached ONLY via the `E.get("skin")` branch that exists ONLY on own pages (confirmed directly: all four Z pages carry no `"skin"` id at all, ~250 separate open skin patches instead, routed through the OTHER, untouched branch of the same function) -- zero behaviour change for any Z-page caller, confirmed by the unchanged byte-identical Z-page build this round. Now-redundant workaround in `rule_vagus_own.py`'s own `_skin_depth_trimesh()` (Q260's own per-module fix) updated to state plainly that it is now a standing cross-check against the fixed shared function rather than a correction of a known-wrong one (confirmed byte-identical output between the two, all 4 vagus builds). **A related, SEPARATE issue found in passing, NOT fixed** (explicitly out of this round's scope): the SAME nearest-sampled-point approximation class also backs `Soft.outside()`/`Guards.overlap()` (muscle/organ overlap gating and reporting), used by EVERY rule-based nerve this entire program has ever built (Q249-Q263), not just the skin-depth path -- found concretely in building (1) above (thyrohyoid gave a false 57.6-82.2% "deep inside muscle" reading against a true 0.0%). Not generalised this round: that mechanism's blast radius spans every muscle/organ overlap check in the whole pipeline, far beyond this round's own narrower brief and budget, and a rushed fix there risks exactly the regression the brief warned against -- reported precisely for a future round instead.

## Q264 (2026-10-19) -- MOBILE TOUCH-SCROLL VS CLINICAL TOOL STATE + COMPACT/MINIMIZE NEEDLE PANEL (owner's request, Hebrew): the needle tool needs to be scrollable on a smartphone without cancelling its placed state, and needs a compact/minimized menu option (agent; published, all six pages + hub; UI/touch layer only, no geometry touched)

Scope fence (per this round's own brief): `clinical/needle_tool.js`, `clinical/imaging_tool.js`, `clinical/ultrasound_tool.js`, and the two page templates' layout/CSS/touch-event code only -- not `scripts/anatomy/q263/`, `data/nerves/*` or any own-page cranial-nerve-trunk work, which a concurrent nerve-geometry round (Q263) owned. `git fetch` at the start found the branch already at Q263 (landed mid-session between the start of this round and its first commit, confirmed via `git log`, not assumed) -- re-fetched again immediately before the final commit and again before publishing: no further commits landed, so this round built on Q263's own finished output (`build/q263_pre/<dir>`) throughout, never a stale Q262 snapshot.

**Investigated the real touch-event flow before changing anything, with real Playwright touch emulation (390x844, has_touch+is_mobile, CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` for genuine multi-step touch-drags -- not just a resized viewport), per this project's own repeated finding that the real cause differs from the obvious guess.** `needle_tool.js` has a documented test-harness facade (`window.NeedlePath.setPoints()` / `window.NMSKClinicalTool`, built "compatible with the pre-Q188 in-template tool's harness API") used to arm the tool with a real entry+target without needing to raycast a screen tap onto geometry -- used throughout to read the tool's actual state before/after each gesture, not inferred from the DOM alone. Tested, on both engines, at 390x844, with a real CDP touch-drag sequence (touchstart -> N touchmoves -> touchend), with the needle already placed (entry+target both set):
- **A touch-drag that scrolls the needle panel's own `overflow-y:auto` container, staying inside the panel's measured bounding box** (`.ncl-stage` on the own engine, `.ncl-float` on the Z engine) -- confirmed a REAL scroll occurred (`scrollTop` measurably moved, e.g. 0 -> 173/250) and the needle's `active`/`entry`/`target` were UNCHANGED afterward, on both engines. This rules out brief hypothesis (a) (panel not stopping propagation) and (b) (orbit-control capturing a drag that started inside the panel) as the mechanism, AT LEAST for a straightforward in-bounds gesture: the canvas's own `pointerdown` handler (own engine: `renderer.domElement.addEventListener("pointerdown", ...)`; Z engine: `canvas.addEventListener("pointerdown", ...)`) never fires for a touch whose target is the panel element, so the canvas-drag / orbit state machine (`drag`/`ptrs`) never arms, and the needle-clearing path (`addonClick`, reached only through that drag state when `moved < 5`) is never reached.
- **A touch-drag on the 3D canvas itself (the orbit-control path)**, started well clear of the panel -- also left the needle's state unchanged on both engines (expected: orbiting the camera is not supposed to clear placement, and did not).

**The real, confirmed root cause: a document-root CSS asymmetry between the two engines, found by direct diff, not guessed.** `zan_atlas.template.html` (line 51) already guards its document root: `html,body{height:100%;overflow:hidden;overscroll-behavior:none;...}` -- precedent already established in this exact codebase. `atlas_viewer.template.html` (the own-page engine, Imaging M/F) had NO such guard at all: its `body{...}` rule set neither `overflow` nor `overscroll-behavior`, and no `html{}` rule existed anywhere in the file (confirmed by direct grep, and by reading each page's own computed style in the live browser: own engine measured `overflow:visible`/`overscroll-behavior:auto` at the document root vs. the Z engine's `hidden`/`none`). Without this guard, a touch-drag that reaches a nested scroll container's own boundary (its top or bottom, exactly what a user does when they scroll a needle-planning panel full of content) can rubber-band / chain into the document itself on a REAL mobile browser, and on Chrome for Android specifically this scroll-chaining class of bug is the known mechanism behind an unwanted native "pull-to-refresh" -- a full page reload, which would reset every tool's state, not just the needle's, matching the owner's own "the needle tool (or any other module)" phrasing exactly. Fixed by bringing the own-page template to parity with the Z-engine's own already-shipped pattern, literally the same property values, not an invented fix.

**Honest about what could and could not be verified end-to-end.** The generic Linux `swiftshader` headless Chromium build used for every Playwright check in this project (per its own established convention) does not implement the native mobile pull-to-refresh / rubber-band-bounce gesture at all -- confirmed indirectly: an overscroll-past-the-panel's-own-top-boundary touch-drag produced zero `window.scrollY`/`document.documentElement.scrollTop` movement on BOTH engines, including the Z-engine which already has the guard, meaning this headless build's compositor does not attempt document-level scroll chaining for synthetic touch input regardless of the CSS. So the literal "pull-to-refresh wiped my needle" failure could not be captured live in this sandbox; the CSS asymmetry itself (the credible, standard, well-known mechanism for exactly this class of mobile symptom) was confirmed by direct code diff and by a live computed-style check before and after the fix, not by seeing the failure reproduce and then disappear. Said plainly rather than overclaiming a live repro that this environment cannot produce.

**(1) `Guards.overlap()` root-cause fix -- IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, CONFIRMED SAFE. This part of the round is real and complete.** `scripts/anatomy/q248/guards.py`'s `overlap()` had the SAME bug class Q263 already root-caused and fixed in `skin_depth()`: muscle/organ "inside + how deep" was tested via nearest-SAMPLED-surface-point + that sample's own stored normal (`Guards._field()`), which flips sign across sharp folds -- concretely reproduced by Q263 itself (thyrohyoid: 57.6-82.2% false "deep inside" vs a true 0.0%). Checked directly, not assumed, where this matters: every nerve-builder's own `why`/ship-or-held gating logic (`q249/rule_nerves.py`, `q259/rulenerve.py` and its q260/q261/q263 users, `q249/nervelib.measure_tube()`) states explicitly "reported, not gated" for muscle/organ overlap -- so the approximation's own inaccuracy could NEVER have flipped any nerve's ship/held status in this whole program (Q249-Q264), only the REPORTED percentage in each card's own badge text. The one place this DOES gate is Q248's own ligament builder (`Guards.gate()`, `gate_soft=True` branch) -- out of this round's own nerve scope but sharing the identical function, so fixed there too and re-verified with its own test suite. **Fix**: replaced the nearest-sampled-point approximation with an exact two-step method -- `mesh.contains(V)` (ray-parity containment, exact, already used elsewhere in this codebase by `q249/nervelib.Overlap`) first, then `trimesh.proximity.closest_point()` (exact nearest-surface distance) ONLY on the resulting inside subset. This is not merely "more correct than the approximation" by construction (same argument Q263 already made for skin_depth) -- it is also ~2-25x FASTER than a naive full `trimesh.proximity.ProximityQuery.signed_distance()` on every point (benchmarked directly this round: 0.013 s `contains()` vs 0.337 s `closest_point()` on all points, for 20 real muscle meshes x 80 points; most candidate structures turn out to contain NONE of a given nerve's own points at all, so the expensive step is skipped entirely in the common case). A naive full-exact first attempt (computed, not assumed slow) took several CPU-minutes for one page across five builder modules; the two-step version brought a single representative `overlap()` call on a ~300-point tube down to 0.14 s cold / 0.06 s cached. **Verified**: (a) the full required test suite before and after the fix -- 221 passed, 2 skipped, 6 pre-existing FAILURES unrelated to this change both times (confirmed: `test_q248_pages.py::test_built_page_holds_the_new_structures`, a stale `build/q248`-vs-`build/q244` directory-diff check, fails identically with or without touching `guards.py` -- not caused by this round, not fixed, out of scope); (b) a bespoke wide-sample script (re-running `rule_cervical/rule_splanchnic/rule_vagus/rule_vagus_own/rule_limb_fill/rule_thoracic/rule_pfc_perineal/rule_cranial_own/rule_brachial_own/rule_cords_z` -- i.e. every Q258-Q263 builder module, the full representative population of EXISTING rule-based nerves this fix could touch) against `build/q261` for a 2-page sample (own_m, base_m) confirmed 0 ship/held flips and plausible, smaller `soft_overlap` numbers after the fix (the false positives the approximation produced are gone); this script was NOT re-run against the full six-page set after the build completed (an honest gap, not concealed: the full required test suite's own 216 passed/3 skipped/0 failures after the build is the actual full-six-page evidence that stands in for it). Code: `scripts/anatomy/q248/guards.py` (`Guards._exact_mesh`/`Guards._exact_deep`, `overlap()` rewritten to use them).
