- **(4) "US diagnostic" preset, `clinical/ultrasound_tool.js`.** A pick-list of four categories (קרע שריר / entrapment עצבי / גיד-רצועה / מפרק-בורסה) tied to the imaging kernel's OWN tissue-class key (muscle / nerve / tendon_ligament / synovial -- `clinical/data/imaging_tissues.json`, not invented) rather than a hand-picked structure list. Selecting a category: reuses the existing Controls show/hide toggle (collapses it, more room for the image), sets `S.cineMode = "continuous"` for THIS preset only (Q257's step cine stays the default everywhere else), pre-sets depth / dynamic range / frequency to typical starting values for that tissue kind (stated as such, not a cited protocol), and -- if a landmark can be found -- centres the probe there via a new `nearestSkin()` helper (casts `LIB.skinHit()`, the exact ray-cast every existing placement already uses, from 14 candidate directions and keeps whichever hit lands closest to the target point; never claimed as anatomically precise, same honesty level as the pre-existing "Screen centre" button). When the category has more than one real candidate on this page (almost always, since muscle/nerve/tendon-ligament/synovial structures number in the dozens to hundreds per body), item 10's wizard strip opens to disambiguate; when it has exactly one, the probe is placed directly; when it has zero, the depth/DR/freq/CINE settings are still applied and the tool says plainly that no landmark was found, probe position unchanged -- never fabricated.
- **(5) A/B side-by-side compare, same file.** A toggle (`S.ab`), not a third "mode": two independent placements (`S.P`/`S.N` and a new `S.P2`/`S.N2`) that share every OTHER control (depth, frequency, gain, rotation, tilt/direction -- literally the same `S.rot`/`S.mTilt`/`S.mTiltDir` the sweep mode's own sliders already expose). Turning it on auto-seeds B as A's point reflected across the body's own midline x, re-seated on the real skin there via the same `nearestSkin()` helper (falls back to "B starts at A's own point, move it manually" when no mirrored skin is found, e.g. a midline-only body region -- never silently fails). Implementation is a genuinely minimal, surgical change to the EXISTING rendering pipeline, not a parallel engine: `poseOf()`, `refFrame()` and `rasterKey()` now take an optional `spec.P`/`spec.N` override (falling back to the single shared `S.P`/`S.N` exactly as before when absent -- star/sweep modes are completely unaffected), and `frameSpecs()` short-circuits to return exactly two specs carrying each slot's own placement when `S.ab` is on; the existing `ensureViews()`/`pump()`/`paintView()`/`annotate()` pipeline needed no further change at all. "Place on skin" now routes to whichever slot (`S.placeSlot`, A/B) is currently armed via a small `placeRay2()` sibling of the existing `placeRay()`. The 3-D overlay shows both probes live at once (not just the selected one) when in A/B mode. A "mirror B <- A" convenience button re-seats B on demand.
- **(6) Opt-in tissue-thickness readout, same file, OFF by default, a SEPARATE toggle from the Q256 source-reliability dots** (different system entirely, `viewer/parts_ui/parts_ui.js` -- confirmed by file, not just by claim). At the hovered point, scans the SAME per-pixel tissue-classification grid (`fr.lab`) the simulation and the existing hover read-out already compute, finds the contiguous run of the same class id through the lateral column, converts to mm by the raster's own pixel size, and shows "Tissue thickness at cursor: <class label> ~ N.N mm (live measurement; no reference range shown)". No "typical range" band is shown or invented: this project has no cited reference range for in-plane ultrasound tissue thickness to compare against (the honest finding Q255 already made for fascia/ligament thickness specifically applies here too), so the live number ships alone, with that limitation stated in the toggle's own tooltip, not glossed over.
- **(7) Reference picture-in-picture panel, `clinical/imaging_tool.js`** (a new, fully self-contained `attachReferencePanel()`, chained onto the existing optional-add-on mechanism in its own try/catch so a failure here can never affect imaging/ultrasound/needle). A floating, draggable (pointer-drag on its own head bar), resizable (native CSS `resize:both`) panel, collapsed to a small toolbar icon by default, reusing the Q264 compact-panel visual idiom (a chevron collapsing the open panel to just its title bar) for its own internal minimize control too. A plain `<input type=file accept="image/*,video/*">` loads a local image or short video clip via `URL.createObjectURL` (a blob: URL) -- **nothing is ever uploaded or fetched over the network for the loaded media**, confirmed by construction (File API + `<img>`/`<video>` + canvas only, exactly as specified). Pan/zoom via a CSS transform on the media wrapper; brightness goes through an actual `<canvas>` (`ctx.filter = "brightness(...)"` + `drawImage`, re-run every animation frame while a video is loaded), not a CSS filter on the media element, per the explicit instruction. Explicitly NOT registration/fusion with the 3-D model: no coordinate mapping, no click-to-align, purely an independent viewer the clinician positions by eye.
- **(8) Injury annotation + read-only reference card, both templates.** Reuses the EXISTING Mark mechanism verbatim (`selCtl.markButton()`, the same factory the structure list's own tick and Q262's per-structure card button already use) -- marking IS the injury flag; a severity cycle (mild / moderate / severe, a new small localStorage map `nmsk.injury.v1`, own-page and Z-engine each keep their own) appears only once the structure is marked, followed by a card explicitly labelled "Reference information -- not a diagnosis or treatment recommendation", pulling ONLY data this project already has: the muscle card's own `nerve`/`targets`/`supplies`/`source` fields (own-page gained `targets`/`supplies` rendering for the first time here, parity with the Z-engine's own already-existing display of the identical fields -- not invented, just not rendered there before); for a nerve with none of its own, the Q256 `plexus_groups.json` sidecar (Q267-extended, see below) gives "branch of" / "innervates" / citation. Degrades to name-only, honestly, when neither source has anything. **A real architectural-invariant violation was caught and fixed before shipping, the exact Q262 lesson re-confirmed by its own test**: the first draft called `selCtl.isMarked(id)` directly from the card-rendering code in BOTH templates to decide whether to show the severity row -- `tests/test_q232.py::test_engines_use_the_display_states` (which bans exactly this pattern outside the selection module) caught it immediately on the Z-engine; fixed in both templates by reading the SAME public `#a-mark` button's own `aria-pressed` attribute instead (kept correct automatically by `selCtl`'s own `syncButtons()`), never reaching into the module's internals -- re-verified green afterward.
  - **Data plumbing for the nerve side, genuinely extended, not invented**: `data/nerves/*.json` already carries a real, cited `targets` field (muscle ids a muscular branch innervates) that `scripts/anatomy/q256/plexus_groups.py` was NOT carrying through into its own derived output; added `targets`/`notes` to that script's per-node dict (one line) and `targets`/`source`/`parent_name` to `scripts/anatomy/q256/build_plexus_sidecar.py`'s per-page sidecar output (one line each) -- re-ran both (`data/derived/Q256_plexus_groups.json` regenerated, same 245-node count, confirmed byte-identical in structure except the new fields; six `plexus_groups.json` page sidecars regenerated as part of the normal publish pipeline below). Confirmed with `tests/test_q256_nerve_groups.py`/`tests/test_q256_attachments.py` still green afterward.
- **(9) One-tap layout toggle, both templates, a new, independent control from the pre-existing `#t-layout` phone/desktop switch.** Cycles Model-only (collapses every clinical-tool Controls panel + the needle tool's own compact toggle, and on the own-page engine shrinks `#app`'s grid to a single column, hiding `aside`/`#inspector`; on the Z-engine, `#rail`/`#info` are already `position:fixed` overlays so simply hiding them already maximises the 3-D view, no grid relayout needed there) / Split (the normal default layout) / Compare (same as Split, except when ultrasound is the open tool, where it nudges item 5's A/B view on). Remembers the last-used layout per active clinical tool (`sessionStorage`, keyed per tool) and auto-returns to Model-only whenever no tool is armed, polled every 500 ms (the same `setInterval` idiom the ultrasound tool's own overlay-tracking poll already uses) rather than a `MutationObserver`, to keep the mechanism simple and match existing convention. **A real, caught-before-shipping architectural violation, a NEW instance of the same class of bug Q262 taught**: the first draft's generic "which tool is armed" check hard-coded the literal tool button ids (`t-ultrasound` among them) directly in the PUBLIC templates -- `tests/test_q228.py::test_public_templates_do_not_mention_ultrasound` (the public pages must never name the private ultrasound add-on) failed immediately, in BOTH templates. Fixed by making tool detection fully generic and private-tool-name-agnostic: it reads the body classes each optional add-on already toggles for its OWN layout CSS (`nmsk-us`, `nmsk-img`, both pre-existing, named nothing newly) and the needle panel's own `hidden` DOM state, never a literal tool name string; and the "Compare -> nudge ultrasound into A/B" direction was inverted architecturally -- the generic template-side code only ever sets a generic `lay-compare` body class, and `clinical/ultrasound_tool.js`'s own existing overlay-poll loop (private code, free to name itself) now watches for that class itself and calls its own `setAb(true)` when it is the open tool. This keeps the public/private boundary exactly where this project's own established convention already draws it (the templates carry only a generic hook; a private add-on may know about the public template, never the other way around). Re-verified green on `test_q228.py` (28 passed) and `test_q232.py` (unchanged failure count, matched against a clean-checkout baseline) after the fix.
- **(10) Guided inline wizard, `clinical/ultrasound_tool.js`, tied to item 4 only.** A thin, dismissible bar (never a modal), shown ONLY when `applyPreset()` finds more than one real candidate for the chosen category (i.e. a genuine disambiguating question exists) -- a search box + a filtered result list, the same visual idiom as the needle tool's own motor-point search (reused as an idiom, not literally shared code, since the two live in separate clinical files); picking a row calls straight into the SAME landmark-centring code path item 4 uses for its single-candidate case, so the wizard's answer lands in the identical manual control (the probe placement) the clinician can immediately override afterward via "Place on skin". Dismissing it leaves the depth/DR/freq/CINE already applied untouched -- only the landmark step is skipped. **Held, explicitly and for the right reason, per the brief's own instruction**: the needle tool's own existing placement modes (entry->target / entry+direction+length / target-first) were NOT given a wizard this round -- they are mode CHOICES, not a disambiguation among many candidates of one fixed kind, so there is no real "which one" question of the shape this wizard answers; forcing one on would have been exactly the "pointless question" the brief says to skip.

Context: Q267 held items 1-3 (vessel-avoidance corridor + trajectory suggestion) pending the owner's own clinical sign-off. The owner answered in writing: build everything, in module-readiness order. The build commit is `17a1c10` (`clinical/needle_tool.js` +416 lines, `viewer/atlas_viewer.template.html` and `viewer/zan_atlas.template.html` +9/-3 each, `tests/test_q268_segment_distance.py`, `scripts/anatomy/q268/verify_ui_q268.py`, `scripts/anatomy/q268/crosscheck_q268.py`, the section-ג bullet in `docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md`). The build session stalled after committing, before publishing, bumping the hub or writing this section; a follow-up agent finished the round from the committed state (what it verified itself vs what it takes from the commit message is marked below).

**Design principle, stated in the code and in the UI**: the tool measures and displays; it never judges "safe / unsafe". Every number the owner might read as a clinical threshold is an editable display default, labelled as such in the panel (`CORR_DEFAULTS = {near: 5, far: 15, R: 40}` in `clinical/needle_tool.js`, with the rationale written beside it).

- **(1) Injection-planning preset.** Structure picker in the needle panel (muscle / tendon search) -> the target plus every vessel / nerve whose bounding box lies within **R = 40 mm** of the target's bounding box is kept, everything else faded through the page's PUBLIC selection-controller API -> origin / insertion markers opened when the page has parts data (and the panel says plainly when it has none) -> needle tool armed target-first; **no point is ever placed for the clinician**. 40 mm rationale (from the code comment): a generous limb-scale neighbourhood of the order of a typical injection depth, chosen so that a path of the default 60 mm needle length does not silently miss a structure lying just beside it -- not a sourced clinical value, editable in the panel. **Spastic-posture toggle**: two labelled, ILLUSTRATIVE postures (`POSTURES.ul` upper-limb flexion pattern, `POSTURES.ll` lower-limb extension + equinovarus pattern), driven only through the Q241 pose rig's own joint ids and clamped by the rig to each page's own normal ranges; joints a page's rig does not carry are reported as skipped, never invented (Imaging pages have no finger joints: 16 angles skipped, per the open-items note). **Held limitation, stated in the UI** (`TP.poseAway()`): the needle tool measures the REST-POSE meshes (the add-on API contract; also a documented pose-rig limitation), so while the pose is away from rest the distance list carries an explicit warning and the numbers are not valid for the displayed body. Measuring on the posed body needs a change to the geometry API contract -- left open.
- **(2) Live distance readout to vessels and nerves.** On every entry / target change: bounding-box prefilter within R, then the exact minimum distance from the entry->target segment (or the single placed point) to every triangle of each candidate mesh (`meshSegDist`, pure functions, exported for tests), listed nearest first with a translucent halo along the path. Two user-editable DISPLAY bands, **5 mm and 15 mm** (near / far), colour the list and are labelled in the panel as display thresholds, not clinical guidance. Cross-check (per the commit message and `scripts/anatomy/q268/crosscheck_q268.py`, which recomputes the same placements independently with trimesh on the same build geometry): **41 distances across 8 placements on 2 pages, worst difference 0.004 mm, no structure missing or extra** -- taken from the build session's run, not re-run by the finishing agent.
- **(3) Suggested entry candidates.** On an explicit "Suggest entries" tap: `coneDirs()` samples `SUGG_N = 48` directions in a `SUGG_HALF_DEG = 35`° cone around the nearest-skin direction (the open-items note counts 49 with the centre direction), each candidate is ranked by its measured minimum clearance (larger first; within `SUGG_TIE_MM = 1.0` mm the shorter path wins), the top `SUGG_SHOW = 2` are drawn as dashed ghosts, **adopted only by an explicit tap**, and when no candidate clears the far band (15 mm or whatever the owner sets) nothing is shown and the panel says so. A plain sampling heuristic, not an optimisation and not a recommendation.
- **Templates (both engines, verified by `git diff 4c89c93 17a1c10`)**: three lazy controller getters on `anatomyApi()` -- `selection()`, `parts()`, `pose()` -- handing the page's own public controller objects to the add-on (they are created after the add-on attaches, hence lazy); and the **Q267 regression fix**: item 9's layout toggle auto-collapsed the needle panel to its title bar on the Model-only init pass and never undid it, so the panel opened collapsed; now a `layNeedleCollapsed` flag undoes ONLY the layout's own auto-collapse when returning to Split / Compare, never a user's Q264 compact choice.

**A. `scripts/regen_template_only.py PAGE... | all --out DIR [--src ROOT] [--ref ROOT] [--expect-changed names] [--allow-disk] [--verify-only]`.** One command for the established chain, in Q270's order and flags: `regen_cut_q218.sh <page>` (SRC_<page>=<src>/<dir>, Q218_OUT=<out>) -> `stage_clinical_files.py --ultrasound` -> `set_titles_q231.py` -> `make_abbrevs.py --inject` -> `make_calibre.py --inject` -> `make_pose_rig.py --inject` -> `build_sidecar.py <q237 key> <dir> -o symmetry_q237.json` -> `build_plexus_sidecar.py --html ... -o plexus_groups.json` -> `index.html` = the page. Refuses an `--out` that is not under `/dev/shm` unless `--allow-disk`. Refuses to continue if `git status --porcelain -- data` changed during a page's build (the make_abbrevs / make_calibre landmine). Then verifies every page against a reference root (default `--src`, i.e. the previous build; `--ref` a dir of downloaded live pages, the service's document skeleton is removed with `platform_wrap.unwrap`): every `<script id="nmsk-*">` block, the own pages' `bundle-json` / `bundle-b64`, the Z pages' `window.__ANATOMY_BIN__ / _BIN_FILES__ / _MANIFEST__` literals byte-identical; every sibling (geo txt, clinical_*, parts_data.json, plexus_groups.json, symmetry_q237.json) sha256-identical unless named in `--expect-changed` (a block id such as `nmsk-imaging-inline`, the pasted clinical code, may be named too; `index.html` there = the page's non-data lines may differ); `<title>` and h1 = the Q231 unified name; `index.html` == the page. Exit 1 with a per-page diff summary (a JSON sibling that differs only in its `generated` date is flagged as such). Default source root `build/q265`. `PARTS_SIDECAR=0` is passed through. ## Q272 (2026-10-20) -- CLINICAL WORKSPACE MODES: the three clinical use-cases became three DISTINCT SCREENS (injection planning / diagnostic US / imaging compare) instead of ten look-alike panels on the anatomy screen, per the owner's "you did not really design the pages" and the approved mockups (artifact TLuuhBc67LVxyLbA3pGdSX); a generic mode layer in the public templates + three private providers that re-skin Q267/Q268's existing logic (agent; published, all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page; no geometry, no new clinical computation)

Context: Q267/Q268 shipped the owner's 10 clinical UI items as small panels crammed into the dense anatomy screen; the owner (a physician) answered "there is no difference between modules. Fix." with a brief for one workspace per use-case: minimal settings, the 3-D model unobstructed, only the needed controls visible, menus collapsible. Mockups (RTL Hebrew) were approved first: a full-screen mode switcher, and three screens -- תכנון הזרקה (teal #0E7C86), US אבחנתי (blue #2B6CB0), השוואת דימות (amber #B5651D) -- each with a 56 px slate mode bar, the mode's own 1-3 cards, a bottom pill row of toggles, and "יציאה למצב אנטומיה".

**A. The mode layer (`viewer/modes/`, public, generic, synced into both templates by `scripts/sync_modes_q272.py` between `MODES <css|html|js|glue> begin/end` markers -- the exact viewer/nerve_groups/ pattern; `tests/test_q272_modes.py` fails if a template drifts).** `modes.html`: the switcher ("מה עושים היום?" with the 4 tiles + the six model chips, dismissable) and the mode shell (bar / main / pills). `modes.css`: `body.mode-on` hides EVERY piece of anatomy chrome of either engine by CSS only (own: header, aside, #inspector, .mob-bar, #tools, #hover, axes/scalebar; Z: #brand, #topright, #rail, #info, #foot, #modal; both: cut panel, labels, parts panel, nerve groups, pose/symmetry banners) -- nothing is destroyed, removing the class restores it; the mode's own colours / cards / pills / page layouts; the 390x844 phone reflow. `modes.js` (`window.NMSKModes`): a registry (`register(key, {title, short, build, enter, exit, refresh})`) the private add-ons call at attach time, `enter(key)` / `exit()`, a snapshot of the anatomy screen taken through public APIs only (camera, selection + marks + group display states via `selCtl.state()/clear()/markIds()/setGroup()`, categories via `api.categoryOn/setCategoryOn`, parts-marker mode, the phone sheets, the Q267 layout-toggle state restored through its own `#t-lay3` button) and its restore on exit, a `dock(el, slot, z)` helper that fixes an existing element (the 3-D canvas, a tool's own panel) onto a slot's rectangle with `!important` inline styles and re-places it on resize / every 300 ms (so no engine or tool DOM is moved or rebuilt), the "מצב" toolbar button, `#mode=<key>` hash support, and a per-session memory (`sessionStorage nmsk.mode.v1`: the switcher shows once per session; the last choice is re-entered on reload). `glue_own.js` / `glue_zan.js`: the host object (the element to dock, the toolbar, `anatomyApi()`, selection get/set, camera snapshot / restore, phone sheets) -- public page functions only. The public templates still never name a private tool (`tests/test_q228.py` + the new test's own guard): a tile whose provider never registers (anatomy-only build) shows "לא זמין בעמוד זה".

**B. The three providers (private, `clinical/*.js`, re-skin only -- every button calls the same function the tool's own panel calls).**
- **תכנון הזרקה** (`clinical/needle_tool.js`, `injectionMode(tool, api)`): model full-bleed; bar chip "מטרה: <structure · side>" + שנה (a picker over the page's own muscles / tendons, `PLAN_CATS`), איפוס / בטל; right step card (1 מטרה ✓ · 2 נקודת כניסה: "הצע נקודות כניסה" = `tool.suggest()` with the ranked candidates listed and adopted by `adoptSuggestion()`, "סמן ידנית על העור" = target-first placement; 3 בדיקת מסלול = `tool.report()`), left distance card (nearest-first rows of `tool.corr.items`, large mm numbers, the colour bar from `tool.band()` at the editable 5 / 15 mm display thresholds, footer "מדידה בלבד · ספי צבע 5 / 15 מ"מ · עריכה" -> `setCorr`), pills הילה / תנוחה ספסטית (cycles the two illustrative Q268 patterns through `applyPosture`, reset on exit) / אחיזות (O/I) (parts markers) / עור (the skin category when the page has one) / שכבות… (category toggles). "As automatic as possible": entering with a muscle already selected on the page adopts it as the target, `planPick()` runs the Q268 preset, and a NEW `TP.setTargetAt(i)` puts a default target point at the structure's vertex centroid (a tap inside the structure replaces it, exactly as before); the tool's own panel (`#needle-panel`) is hidden by CSS in the mode but keeps running (its 3-D overlays, its state); `TP.hooks` / `TP.notify()` (called at the end of update / renderCorridor / renderSuggestions / planPick / planRelease / clear) drive the cards. - **השוואת דימות** (`clinical/imaging_tool.js`, `compareMode(api)`): pane "דימות המטופל" = Q267's reference picture-in-picture panel `#ref-root` docked (its own bars hidden; "החלף קובץ" = its file input, זום / בהירות = `NMSKReference.set`, "נטען מקומית · לא נשלח"), pane "האטלס — חתך תואם" = the page's own simulation docked (US chip -> the ultrasound companion, CT / MRI -> this tool with `set({modality})`, both in their `tab` layout) or the 3-D model ("תלת-ממד"), the centre "זום משותף" lock = the reference zoom applied as a CSS scale (+ clip) to the atlas pane -- a DISPLAY zoom, said so; bottom injury bar = structure picker, three severity pills that go through the page's EXISTING Mark mechanism (`sel.mark()` via the public API, then the page's own `[data-sev]` buttons in `#i-injury` / `#inj-card`) and the collapsed "מידע רפרנס (עצבוב, אספקה) — לא אבחנה ▸" drawer that shows the page's own read-only reference card. Honest limit, stated in the UI: no "matching slice" exists as data -- the atlas pane is the simulation at the probe / plane the user positions ("סימולציה מהמשים").

Verification -- real headless Chromium, `scripts/anatomy/q272/verify_modes.py OWN_DIR ZAN_DIR --shots DIR` (extends verify_ui_q267's approach): Imaging M (own engine) + Base M (Z engine) at 1400x900 and 390x844 = 4 passes, 132 OK / 0 FAIL, 0 page errors.** Per pass: the switcher appears on first load with all three providers registered and dismisses; "מצב" reopens it; entering each mode sets its body class and the rail / details / toolbar are NOT visible (computed-style + rect), the mode bar / cards / pills are; injection: target adopted or picked -> default target point -> the distance card already reads the neighbourhood -> suggest -> adopt -> readout "segment" + step-3 report (on Base M no candidate cleared the 15 mm far threshold for the auto-picked target, the tool's own message is shown -- not a failure); US: preset applied (4 cm / 55 dB / 12 MHz, continuous) with CINE running, status chip + badge, A/B on with a second placement; compare: a local PNG through the reference panel's File input, zoom lock -> CSS scale follows, severity "בינונית" through the page's own card, the reference drawer labelled "not a diagnosis"; exit: a visibility snapshot of the chrome, the camera, the marks and the selection compared before / after (equal) and the tools closed again when they were closed before. ## Q273 (2026-10-21) -- POLISH ROUND ON THE THREE WORKSPACE MODES: six small defects from Q272's own screenshots and its "rough / held" list, no new feature, no geometry, no clinical computation (agent; published all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page)

2. **A/B with no skin contact**: `setAb()` / `mirrorBtoA()` oriented B's normal "away from A's mirror image"; when that image lies outside the body (an arm hanging away from the trunk) the probe was inverted -> NO SKIN CONTACT. New `seatMirrorB()` (clinical/ultrasound_tool.js) seats B on the skin nearest to the mirror image through the Q267 `nearestSkin()` helper and orients the normal by the ray that found the skin (always from outside, `h.out`); `S.abSnapMm` records the snap distance and the CINE bar says "B הוצמד לעור הקרוב בצד הנגדי (N מ"מ מנקודת המראה)" when > 5 mm. NOT verifiable here: whether claude.ai's artifact wrapper forwards the hash / query to the page frame (the wrapper's frame-shell script is behind the blocked assets proxy); the hub links keep `#mode=`, and the switcher still appears on first load if nothing reaches the page. ## Q274 (2026-10-21) -- TWO SEPARATE OWNER REPORTS: Base · Female "missing a lot" (pipeline bug, found and fixed) + four mobile symptoms, investigated with real touch-emulated Playwright, one convention-gap fix shipped, root cause only partially confirmed (agent; published all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page)

**(1) Base · Female content gap -- quantified against every male counterpart, found to be a pipeline bug, not a source gap.** Cross-checked data/derived sidecar counts class by class, not just looking at the rendered page: Imaging-based (own_m/own_f) -- `parts_data.json` counts.structures 114/122 (F has MORE, not fewer); Combined (zan_m/zan_f) -- 152/152 structures, 229/233 valid origin/insertion placements (parity, F slightly ahead). Only Base (zan_atlas/base_female) showed a real asymmetry: 518/518 parts and 151/151 structures identical (same generic Z body, as documented since Q196/Q250), but Base F's own `parts_data.json` `geometry.placements_valid_on_this_page` was only 99/234 (135 of 234 origin/insertion markers silently dropped to text-only) against Base M's 234/234 (0 dropped). Root-caused, not assumed: `scripts/anatomy/q219/geomlib.py`'s `BODIES["zbase_f"]` path was hardcoded to `build/q218/viewer_base_female/...` -- a snapshot predating Q250's female-pelvis skeleton warp and Q252's CVH-perineal additions. `data/derived/Q220_parts_zbase_f.json` (last regenerated at Q256, commit 68b876e, for the origin/insertion-table extension, unrelated to this bug) was therefore computed against pre-Q250 mesh positions; `build_parts_sidecar.py`'s own per-page geometry check (verifying each placement against the live page's current meshes, tolerance ~7-20 mm) correctly caught the drift and fell back 135/234 markers to text-only. `zbase_m`'s own hardcoded path (also `build/q218`) never broke because the male base skeleton never moved after Q218 -- masking the asymmetry as "only the female page is missing things" when it was a one-sided stale-reference bug, the same bug class as Q271's dropped `set_titles_q231.py` step. The 87 affected structures (clavicle, gluteus medius/minimus, ACL/PCL, hamstrings, several ligaments and fasciae, lateral femoral cutaneous n.) are shared-body structures present on both sexes, not female organs -- confirming this was never a genuine source gap. **Fix** (one line + one regen): `geomlib.py`'s `zbase_f` path repointed to `build/q265/viewer_base_female/...` (the current reference build `regen_template_only.py` already uses); `data/derived/Q220_parts_zbase_f.json` regenerated (`scripts/anatomy/q219/build_geometry.py --bodies zbase_f --skip-validation`, since the full `--bodies` validation path needs the fitted Z bodies, not zbase); re-checked directly against the live page geometry: 234/234 valid, 0 dropped -- exact parity with Base M (518 parts, 151 structures, 342 meshes_with_parts, 234 placements, 120 parts_placed, identical on both pages). `tests/test_q220.py`'s own `page_html()` (pinned only to the original Q220-round `build/q220`/`build/q218` snapshots) updated to prefer `build/q265` first -- the same "repoint the stale build-source pointer after a deliberate geometry change" precedent Q250/Q263 already set for other scripts; without this the test's own fixture would now fail against the corrected derivation. **Genuine, still-open (a)-class gaps, re-confirmed, not re-litigated**: `clitoris_cavernous_body` on Base F stays honestly held (real ~5 mm bone penetration, Q252); round ligaments of the uterus and superior rectal vessels (Q250) remain out.

**(2) Mobile bug report, broken into the owner's four stated symptoms, investigated with real Playwright BEFORE any fix** (390x844, `has_touch`/`is_mobile`, raw CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` touchstart/move/end -- not `.click()`, which the project's own existing `verify_modes.py` uses for its phone-viewport checks and which does NOT reproduce this). Build used for all live checks: `scripts/regen_template_only.py all --out /dev/shm/q274 --src build/q265` -> REGEN_TEMPLATE_ONLY_OK (byte-identical data blocks).
- **"Can't go back" (exit button) -- reproduced with real touch dispatch on the own-engine (Imaging) page, both before and after the fix; the project's own `verify_modes.py` cannot see this because it exits via `.click()`, not `.tap()`.** With the mode genuinely entered (confirmed via `NMSKModes.state().cur`, not a flat timeout) and the page fully rendered (screenshot evidence: the US B-mode panel, CINE bar, distance cards all correctly drawn), a real `.tap()` on `#mb-exit-x` (the phone-only exit "X") reliably timed out across all three modes (inj/us/cmp) on Imaging M; the identical `.tap()` on Base M (Z-engine) succeeded immediately, no code change needed. Ruled out as the cause: CSS stacking (the hit-test target resolves correctly to the button's own child, confirmed via `elementFromPoint`); the mode switcher being left open (confirmed dismissed via `NMSKModes.state().switcherOpen === false` before each attempt). Found one real, confirmed convention gap: `viewer/modes/modes.css` is the only place in both templates' entire interactive-control surface lacking `touch-action:manipulation` -- every other panel (`#cut-panel`, `#pm-panel`, `#lab-panel`, `#sel-sec`, `#ng-panel` buttons) already declares it defensively. **Fixed**: one declaration added to the shared `:where(#mode-switch,#mode-shell) button{...}` rule (covers the switcher tiles, the mode-bar buttons including `#mb-exit-x`, and every `.mc-*`/`.mm-*`/`.mp` button, since all are literal `<button>` elements under that selector), re-synced into both templates via the existing `scripts/sync_modes_q272.py --check` (clean). **Honestly not fully root-caused**: `#sel-markmode` (plain anatomy mode's own "Mark by clicking" button, which already had `touch-action:manipulation` from the pre-existing `#sel-sec button{...}` rule) ALSO failed a real `.tap()` in the same test session -- meaning touch-action alone does not explain every observed failure, and I could not get a clean, decisive re-confirmation specifically isolating the fix's effect on the own engine: this sandbox's software-rendered (swiftshader, no GPU) headless Chromium took 60-150+ seconds to fully decode and render the Imaging pages' embedded geometry in repeated clean (uncontended) runs, far slower than the Z-engine pages, and several multi-minute live-Playwright passes were needed before this was understood -- a genuine test-harness/environment limit, stated plainly rather than claimed as a clean pass. Required suite unaffected by the fix: `tests/test_q272_modes.py` + `test_q226.py` + `test_q228.py` 69 passed/4 skipped before and after.

## Q275 (2026-10-21) -- MOBILE INVESTIGATION CLOSED OUT: Q274's four owner symptoms resolved for real, with a genuine "page fully ready" wait instead of a flat timeout, replacing guesswork with measurement (agent; published all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page; UI/test-infrastructure only, no geometry, no clinical logic)

**Real timing measured first, before touching anything.** Built a precise ready-wait (`document.readyState==="complete"` + a settled double-`requestAnimationFrame` + the same completion signal `smoke_check.py`/`verify_modes.py` already use, `window.NMSKImaging.ready()`) and timed it on both engines at 390x844, repeatedly: ~9 seconds end to end on both the own (Imaging) and Z (Base/Combined) engines -- not 60-150 seconds as Q274 estimated. That earlier estimate was itself substantially a test-harness artifact: this round's own first-pass script reproduced a near-identical-looking ~30-40s inflation from a single wrong CSS selector in its own wait condition (`#sel-sec .row` instead of `#list .row`), the same shape of self-inflicted slowdown Q274's own methodology likely suffered from.

**"Menus don't open/scroll" (owner items 2) and "can't mark" / "can't change colour" (items 1, 3) -- ALL THREE a single real, confirmed, root-caused CSS bug, now fixed, not a timing artifact.** Root cause, found by reading the live pages' own CSS directly (all six currently-published pages carried it, confirmed by reading each): Q267's "Model-only" one-tap layout (`applyPanelLayout("model")`, called unconditionally at page init on every single load, on both engines, since there is no clinical tool armed yet) sets `#app.lay-model aside,#app.lay-model #inspector{display:none}` on the own engine and `body.lay-model #rail,body.lay-model #info{display:none!important}` on the Z engine -- and NOTHING ever overrode `display` back for the phone bottom-sheet "open" state that Q197/Q270 built. The phone sheet's own open/close mechanism (`transform`+`visibility`) was therefore defeated from underneath on every single phone page load: tapping "Structures & layers" correctly toggled every class (`open`, `phone`, `sheet-open` -- confirmed via `getComputedStyle`) but `display` stayed `none`, so the panel (and with it `#sel-markmode` and `#sel-hl`, both living inside it) was never actually visible to tap, scroll or use, regardless of touch vs click, regardless of load timing. **Fixed narrowly, phone-scoped only**: `viewer/atlas_viewer.template.html`'s `#app.phone aside,#app.phone #inspector{...}` rule gained `display:block` (same specificity as the lay-model rule, wins by coming later in the stylesheet -- the standard CSS cascade precedent this project already uses elsewhere); `viewer/zan_atlas.template.html` gained two new rules inside its existing phone media query: `body.lay-model #rail.open{display:flex!important}` and `body.lay-model #info:not(.hidden){display:block!important}`. Desktop Model-only behaviour (intentionally hiding the side panels to maximise the 3-D view) is untouched on both engines. **Verified end to end with real `.tap()`/`page.touchscreen.tap()`, never `.click()`, on a confirmed-ready page**: the panel opens at real nonzero size (390x523 px own engine, 390x520 px Z engine, not 0x0), a real CDP touch-drag gesture scrolls it (`scrollTop` 698->945, own engine; overflow confirmed 16800+ px of content), a real tap on "Mark by clicking" flips `markMode` true/false on both engines (`window.__selState().markMode`), `#sel-hl` hit-tests to itself via `elementFromPoint` and a real `input` event on it reaches `selCtl.state().hl` -- the exact variable the renderer's own one-line colour-setting code (`m.material.color.setHex(... hlc ? selCtl.hlHex() ...)`, read directly, not assumed) already consumes. Honest limitation, same on every round that ever tested this: headless Chromium cannot drive the native OS colour-picker popup a real tap on `<input type=color>` opens, so the very last visual mile is unverifiable here; the reachability and the code path from the `input` event to the renderer are verified instead.

**"Can't go back" (owner item 4, the exit button) -- CLARIFIED, not a touch/CSS bug at all; Q274's apparent tap failure was never a hit-test or dispatch problem.** Instrumented `#mb-exit-x`'s own click listener directly (a counter bound on the element itself, independent of any subsequent app state): a real tap fired it **immediately, every single attempt, with zero misses**, across dozens of trials, both engines, all three clinical modes (inj/us/cmp). `elementFromPoint` confirmed the tap always lands on the button or its own child (the SVG icon), never on a covering element. What varied between attempts was how long `NMSKModes.exit()`'s own subsequent synchronous work (`undockAll()` + `restoreSnapshot()` + `draw()`, which re-colours/re-opacifies every structure on the page) takes to actually finish and set `cur` back to `null`: a steady ~0.7s on the Z engine in every trial, but ranging 0.7s-21+s on the own (Imaging) engine across repeated, otherwise-identical runs in this same session -- not deterministically tied to any specific precondition tested (tried isolating "after marking/colour-change" vs a fresh page; both showed the same wide variance). This tracks background main-thread contention from the clinical imaging/ultrasound geometry pipeline under this sandbox's software (swiftshader, no GPU) rendering -- the same class of environment limitation this project's own `clinical/ultrasound_tool.js` Q257 comment already documents (rAF/BeginFrame unreliable here, hence that file's own `setTimeout`-based frame loop) -- not any identifiable code defect, touch-dispatch gap, or CSS issue. Left open, correctly, as a disclosed test-environment characteristic rather than inventing a fix for a non-bug; cannot be confirmed from here whether or how much this manifests on a real phone.

**New test script**: `scripts/anatomy/q275/mobile_q275_check.py` -- real touch-dispatch (`page.touchscreen.tap()` / CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` for drags, never `.click()`) end-to-end check for both engines: the ready-signal timing above, mode-switcher dismissal, panel-open geometry (polled over time, not a single flat read, to avoid judging mid-CSS-transition), mark-toggle, colour-input reachability + public-state change, a real touch-drag scroll, and all three clinical-mode exit buttons with click-fired-immediately and exit-completed-in-time measured as two separate, non-conflated signals. Its own header documents the actual lesson of this round in both directions: `.click()` cannot be trusted for phone-viewport exit/mark-toggle checks (misses real CSS-visibility bugs that only show up under `.tap()`'s actionability path), but `.locator().tap()`'s own actionability/"stability" pre-check can ALSO itself produce a false "failure" against a page whose layout reflows every ~300ms (this page's own mode-bar refresh tick) even though a real finger does not wait for DOM stability -- `page.touchscreen.tap()` (lower-level, no pre-check) is what this round settled on for the exit-button check specifically.

## Q278

Direct continuation of Q277. Owner uploaded 5 Thingiverse model downloads (zip, pre-extracted) plus a teachmeanatomy.info link, in response to Q277's report on the still-blocked labia/mons/vulvar-skin/ovarian-vessel/real-breast gaps. Job: real forensic + provenance verification before any use, applying the Kiesel 2022 precedent (clean CC-BY license is not evidence of real geometry).

**The 5 models**: gaudi `thing:3876016` "Anatomic Clitoris" (CC-BY) · AMS3188 `thing:1498267` "Anatomical Clitoris" (CC-BY) · AMS3188 `thing:1498289` "External Sex Organs" (CC-BY) · AMS3188 `thing:1498280` "Uterus, Vagina, Internal Sex Organs" (CC-BY) · mbcomputerservices `thing:1154961` "Female Pelvis and Sacrum" (CC-BY-SA, share-alike).

**Mesh forensics (trimesh, `scripts` kept outside the untrusted extracted-zip dir, `python3 -I`)**: loaded all 5 STLs plus 3 real CVH/Wu-et-al-2015 segmented reference meshes of comparable pelvic-region scale already in the project (`third_party/cvh_wu2015/meshes/22_Bartholin_s_gland.ply`, `37_Bulbospongiosus_muscle.ply`, `24_Perineal_body.ply`), with vertex welding (`process=True`) so face-adjacency/dihedral-angle stats are meaningful. Measured mean face-adjacency dihedral angle (the surface-roughness signature): real CVH meshes = 27.6°-31.7° (std 34°-36°) -- vs the 5 uploaded models = 4.7°-17.6° (std 6.5°-22.3°), i.e. **2-6x smoother than real marching-cubes-segmented tissue**, the same "artificially smooth" signature as the rejected Kiesel 2022 model. The pelvis STL (`female_pelvis_fixed.stl`) is also extremely low-poly for a whole bony pelvis+sacrum: 5,556 faces total (orders of magnitude below real bone-segmentation density elsewhere in this project). STL raw-unit bbox for the pelvis (10.8x5.4x8.2) is ambiguous as a standalone signal -- plausible real pelvis dimensions IF the file's native unit is inches (10.8in=274mm etc.), so scale alone was correctly NOT used as evidence either way; the dihedral-angle finding is the real quantified signal.

**Provenance research**: thingiverse.com, amystenzel.wix.com and teachmeanatomy.info are all DNS-unreachable from this sandbox (same restriction Q277 already documented) -- could not read the creators' pages or profiles directly. WebSearch found that the same genre of hobbyist clitoris models (not these exact files, but the same creator community) is explicitly described elsewhere as "based on the work of Di Marino & Lepidi 2014" -- an atlas/descriptive paper, not raw patient imaging -- and confirmed the real Geneva MRI-derived models (Abdulcadir et al. 2020, Q277 row 12) are hosted on unige.ch's OWN separate Thingiverse account, not gaudi's or AMS3188's. For the pelvis: the creator's own README is the decisive textual evidence -- explicit first-person admission of starting from an existing MALE pelvis print and hand-editing it by eye after watching YouTube videos ("Can't tell the difference? Neither could I"), not from any female-specific scan.

**Verdict: all 5 rejected as illustrative/hand-modeled**, same problem class as Kiesel 2022, regardless of their clean CC-BY/CC-BY-SA licenses. Nothing built, no page touched, no republish, no test run needed (no code/geometry path touched). Checked the 3 already-uploaded PDFs: the Visible Korean Human female-pelvis paper (Chung et al. 2020, s12565-020-00562-y) confirms real cadaveric female-pelvis sectioned/segmented data exists at Ajou University but states no explicit license in its abstract/intro -- adds no new fact to the already-pending row 4 decision, which correctly stays with the owner.

**docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md**: new row 15 (section א) logging the full forensic verdict in detail so this exact file set is never re-investigated from scratch; section ב got a new dated Q278 paragraph re-confirming the labia/mons/clitoris/pelvis gaps remain unfilled after this genuine check. `git status` after this round's edits should show only `docs/OPEN_ITEMS_FOR_OWNER.md` and this file.

## Q281 (2026-10-25) -- THREE NEW OWNER REQUESTS: motor points (NMJ) shown only for marked muscles, an "expected injection zone" in the injection-planning preset (origin/insertion/MTJ/fascial-passage + NMJ together, per bundle), and a new multi-slice cross-section sub-module in Cut mode (agent; published all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page; UI/interaction only, no geometry)

**A. Motor points (NMJ) only for marked muscles (`clinical/needle_tool.js`).** `TP.emphasize()`'s "Emphasize motor points" toggle used to show every motor point in `clinical_motor_points.json` regardless of selection. Added `TP.markedIds()` (reads the existing Q227 Marked-structures set via `api.selection().state().marks`, the project's own established multi-select vocabulary -- no second selection mechanism built) and `TP.visibleMpPoints()` (filters `this.mp.points` by that set; a selection controller present but nothing marked shows 0 points -- the literal reading of "only in the selected muscles" -- a page with no selection controller at all falls back to the old unfiltered behaviour). `TP.emphasize()`/`TP.onHostChange()` were split: `TP.refreshMpOverlay()` redraws the sphere overlay for the current `mp.on` state only; `emphasize()` calls it plus `applyOverride()` exactly once when the toggle flips, `onHostChange()` (fired by the host's own `apply()`/`draw()` cycle whenever marks change) calls only `refreshMpOverlay()`. **Real bug caught and fixed in development, not shipped**: the first version had `onHostChange()` call `emphasize(true)` again, which calls `applyOverride()` -> `api.setOpacityOverride()` -> the host's `apply()` -> its own `changeHooks.forEach()` -> `onHostChange()` again -- infinite recursion, `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` in a real browser, caught via a standalone Playwright repro before it reached the shared verify script. New panel line (`#ncl-mp-sel-msg`) states "showing every motor point" (no selection controller), the marked count, or a hint to mark a muscle first.

**B. "Expected injection zone" in the injection-planning preset (`clinical/needle_tool.js`, `viewer/parts_ui/parts_ui.js`).** `TP.planPick()` (the existing "pick a target to plan an injection into") already fades everything but the target+neighbours and shows its origin/insertion Parts markers. Added `TP.planZone()`/`TP.renderPlanZone()`/`TP.drawPlanMp()`: picking a target now also shows, together, its bundles/heads (origin/insertion/MTJ/fascial-passage parts grouped by their real `structure_parts.json` `part_set` -- this project's own bundle concept, e.g. `deltoid.heads`'s 3 named heads) and its own motor point(s) (NMJ, drawn via a dedicated overlay independent of Part A's global toggle -- planning a target always shows THAT target's NMJ regardless of what else is marked). Two small additions to `viewer/parts_ui/parts_ui.js` (synced into both templates via the existing `scripts/sync_parts_ui_q220.py`, no new sync script needed): `partsFor(meshId)` (a structure's parts grouped by part_set, side-independent, without touching the Parts card's own `sel` state) and `focusById(partId)` (focus one named part's marker by id, the same action a card-row click already does, callable from outside). Wired into both skins: the bare tool's own panel (`#ncl-plan-zone`, new) and the Hebrew `mode-inj` card (`אזור ההזרקה הצפוי`, reading `tool.plan.zone` cached once per `planPick()` call, not recomputed). **Coverage, stated plainly, not glossed over**: cross-referencing `clinical/data/motor_points.json` (59 structures with >1 motor point) against `data/anatomy/structure_parts.json`'s `part_sets` of type `head_belly` (22 structures) gives exactly 12 muscles with BOTH a named bundle grouping and multi-point NMJ data (full four-category coverage): `adductor_magnus`, `biceps_brachii`, `biceps_femoris`, `brachialis`, `brachioradialis`, `deltoid`, `flexor_digiti_minimi_brevis_hand`, `gastrocnemius`, `pectoralis_major`, `supinator`, `triceps_brachii`, `vastus_medialis`. ~20 more muscles (`fibularis_brevis`/`longus`, `rectus_femoris`, `semitendinosus`/`semimembranosus`, `tibialis_anterior`/`posterior`, `trapezius`, etc.) have multi-point NMJ data but no documented bundle grouping -- their zone shows the whole-muscle parts list (not per-bundle) plus the motor points. ~10 muscles (`masseter`, `temporalis`, `levator_ani`, etc.) have a documented bundle grouping but zero motor-point data -- the panel says so ("no motor-point data for this structure"), nothing invented. Deltoid's 3 motor points are labelled "anterior/middle/posterior belly" by reading each point's OWN cited rule text (Yi et al. 2023 literally names the belly in its `source.rule` field) via `mpBundleLabel()` -- a text match on the point's own citation, never a fabricated index-to-bundle mapping; muscles whose motor-point text doesn't name a part get "Point k of N", not a guessed label.

**C. Multi-slice cross-section (`viewer/cut_cap/cut_cap.js`, `viewer/cut_mode/cut_mode.html`+`.css`).** New: `NMSKCrossSectionCore.planesFor()` (pure layout math: N=3-12 parallel planes centred on Cut mode's current plane, spaced by an adjustable step, each optionally a near+far pair when thickness>0 -- same semantics as Cut mode's own existing slice-thickness slab, generalised) and `NMSKCrossSection(E)` (the controller: panel, debounced rebuild, mouse-wheel/touch-drag spacing). Reuses `NMSKCapCore.build()` (Q227's real per-structure triangle/plane-intersection + even-odd scanline fill) once per plane -- genuinely N (or 2N with thickness) real cross-sections, not one slice redrawn. Reuses the engine's own existing per-face quad/texture pool (`capUpload`/`capFaces` on the own-engine template, `capUpload`/`capGL` on the Z-engine) via `uploadFace`/`showFace` adaptor methods, under its own slot namespace (`FACE_BASE = 900`) so it can never collide with Cut mode's own faces 0/1 -- no new rendering code needed in either engine. New UI lives inside the existing `#cut-panel` (not a separate toolbar button/panel): a "Multi-slice cross-section" toggle + slice-count/step/thickness number inputs + step nudge buttons, all behind Cut mode being on (refuses cleanly with an explanatory message and 0 faces built when Cut mode is off, verified both by direct call and by the message text). Scroll (mouse wheel) or a one-finger touch-drag over the panel changes the step between slices, independent of thickness. `window.xsecCtl` exposed explicitly on both templates (own-engine: genuinely global; Z-engine: the only one of its controllers exposed outside its IIFE) as a deliberate test/harness hook, same convention as `window.NMSKClinicalTool`/`window.NeedlePath`.

## Q282 (2026-10-25) -- OWNER CLARIFICATION OF THE GOAL BEHIND Q281: not "more features", but "any user should be able to produce what they want in minimum time and clicks" -- worked example given verbatim: 5mm-spaced axial cross-sections of the right hand, abbreviated labels, highlighting FPL (flexor pollicis longus) including its motor point (agent; published all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page; UI composition only, no geometry, no new mechanism duplicated)

**A. Investigation (before writing any code).** Mapped the exact friction in the shipped (post-Q281) viewer for the owner's worked scenario: (1) orientation presets (sagittal/axial/coronal, `viewer/cut_mode/cut_mode.html`) and the Q281 multi-slice stack were already 1-2 actions each but required Cut mode to be opened and the plane positioned by hand ("Place on model" + a click on the model, or the slider/arrow keys) -- no "centre on this structure" existed anywhere. (2) There was NO general "focus the camera on a searched structure" action outside the clinical Needle tool's own `ncl-zoom` and the Parts-marker click handler (`viewer/parts_ui/parts_ui.js`) -- `select(id)` in both templates never moves the camera. (3) Marking + highlighting a structure required the Marked-structures section (`viewer/selection/selection.html`, `#sel-markcur`) *and* the separate Q232 preset (`#sel-p-hlsel`) in the same panel, but reaching it needs the rail open first on the Z-engine pages (pre-existing Q267 "Model only" default, out of scope here). (4) The Q281 marked-filtered NMJ toggle (`#ncl-mp-on`) lives inside the clinical Needle tool panel specifically, conceptually about injection planning, not plain anatomy browsing. (5) Abbreviated labels take 2-3 actions in the existing Labels panel (`viewer/labels/labels.html`, `#lab-show`+`#lab-text`) -- judged acceptable as-is. Confirmed via `api.focus(p,d)` (already on `anatomyApi()` in both templates, the exact primitive the clinical tool's own "Zoom" button already calls) and `selCtl.mark(id,on)`/`selCtl.preset("hlsel")` (already public methods on the Q227 selection controller, used verbatim by `TP.planPick` in `clinical/needle_tool.js`) that no new camera-framing, marking, or highlighting primitive was actually needed -- only a thin composing panel plus two trivial API exposures.

**B. Built: `viewer/quickview/` (quickview.html/.css/.js), a new "Quick view" composer, one shared module for both engines.** `NMSKQuickView(api)` takes the SAME `anatomyApi()` object the optional clinical add-on attaches to (not a narrower adaptor) and is instantiated unconditionally (`quickCtl = NMSKQuickView(anatomyApi());`, `window.quickCtl` exposed as a test hook, same convention as `window.xsecCtl`) right after the clinical-attach line in both templates -- it is public and always present, unlike the optional clinical layer. New toolbar button `#t-quick` opens a small panel: a search box filtering `api.list()` by name/id; picking a result shows **Focus** (`api.focus(mid(r), max(160, ext(r)*1.6))`, the exact formula `TP.planPick` already uses), **Mark & highlight** (`sel.mark(id,true); sel.preset("hlsel")`, reused verbatim, no second marking mechanism), three orientation buttons (sagittal/axial/coronal) that call `api.setCut({normal, point:mid(r)})` -- which positions Cut mode's plane AND turns the panel visible in one call (`cutCtl.setFromSpec` already does `S.on=true; push()`) -- plus `api.crossSection().set(true)` to turn on the Q281 multi-slice stack centred there in the same action; an abbreviated-labels checkbox calling `api.labels().setMode("sel")`/`.set("text","abbr")` (Q236 controller, reused verbatim); and, gated on `window.NMSKClinicalTool.emphasize` existing AND that specific structure having real motor-point data (`tool.mp.points.some(p => p.structure_id === id)`, checked, never assumed) -- **Show its motor point**, which marks the structure if needed and calls `tool.emphasize(true)` directly, the same Q281 marked-filtered mechanism. Two trivial, additive API exposures made this possible without duplicating anything: `anatomyApi()` in both templates gained `labels:function(){return labelsCtl;}, crossSection:function(){return xsecCtl;}` (same lazy-handover convention already used for `selection()`/`parts()`/`pose()`); `viewer/cut_cap/cut_cap.js`'s `NMSKCrossSection` return object gained `setN:setN, setSpacing:setSpacing, setThickness:setThickness` (the same internal functions its own number inputs already call). New sync script `scripts/sync_quickview_q282.py` (same marker-splice pattern as `sync_cut_mode_q197.py`/`sync_q227.py`) keeps `viewer/quickview/*` identical in both templates.

**C. Measured, not estimated: the before/after click count for the owner's own worked scenario.** Built the pre-Q282 baseline by `git stash` (clean revert to the Q281 commit), rebuilding Base M (`viewer_zan_atlas`, confirmed to carry both `flexor_pollicis_longus_r` and its own motor-point datum before picking it -- not assumed) through the existing `scripts/regen_template_only.py` pipeline, then running a real Playwright script against it performing the identical end state (axial plane centred on FPL, multi-slice on, 5mm spacing, FPL marked+highlighted, abbreviated labels showing it, its motor point shown) via the OLD panels only: **16 discrete actions** across four separate panels (layout toggle to open the rail -> search+select in the main list -> Mark selected -> Highlight selected preset -> open Cut panel -> axial preset -> "Place on model" arm + a click on the model -> turn on multi-slice -> type the 5mm spacing -> open Labels panel -> Show=Selected -> Text=Abbreviation -> open the Needle tool panel -> Emphasize motor points). Then `git stash pop` to restore the Q282 working tree and ran the identical scenario through the new Quick view panel on the same freshly-rebuilt page: **9 discrete actions**, all from one panel (open Quick view -> type search query -> pick FPL(r) from the results, disambiguated by its own id text since the list shows identical "Flexor pollicis longus" text for both sides -> Focus -> Mark & highlight -> axial button -> type 5mm spacing, the one remaining shared numeric field the panel auto-opens -> abbreviated-labels checkbox -> Show its motor point). Confirmed the end state matched exactly: `xsecCtl.state()` -> `{on:true, n:5, spacing:5, thickness:0}`, `labelsCtl.state()` -> `{mode:"sel", text:"abbr", shown:["flexor_pollicis_longus_r"]}`, `NMSKClinicalTool.visibleMpPoints()` -> `["flexor_pollicis_longus_r"]` only. A real regression, not a guess: 16 -> 9 actions (44% fewer), and the panel-hopping collapses from four panels to one (plus the shared Cut-panel spacing field it opens automatically).

**D. A real process bug caught mid-round, not shipped.** Editing the shared source `viewer/cut_cap/cut_cap.js` directly (to add the three setter exposures) without re-running its OWN existing sync script, `scripts/sync_q227.py`, left both templates carrying a stale copy of that file -- caused 8 new test failures (`test_q227.py` x3, `test_q232.py` x2, `test_q236_labels.py`, `test_q249_units.py::test_every_sync_script_still_reports_up_to_date`, `test_q256_nerve_groups.py`) on top of the known 11 pre-existing ones, caught by running the full suite before publishing (not skipped). Root-caused to the missed sync step (not a code defect) and fixed by running `scripts/sync_q227.py`, which restored every sync script to "up to date" and the suite to exactly the pre-existing 11 failures.

**E. Verification.** New `scripts/anatomy/q282/verify_q282.py` (real headless Chromium via Playwright, `verify_q276.py`/`verify_q281.py`'s established pattern): panel open/search/pick; Focus and Mark&highlight report success; axial button turns Cut mode + multi-slice on in one action and reaches exactly 5mm spacing; abbreviated-labels checkbox reaches `text:"abbr"`; motor-point button is enabled only for a structure with real data (checked against `flexor_pollicis_longus_r`, confirmed present on BOTH `vhf`/Imaging F and `zan_m`/Base M before testing) and shows exactly that structure's own point; a bone (verified to have no motor-point data) does not falsely offer the button. Both engines (own via Imaging F, Z via Base M), both viewports (1400x900 real click, 390x844 real touch via `touchscreen.tap`), 0 page errors -- **ALL OK**. Full `tests/` suite after the Part-D fix: **11 failed / 1715 passed / 135 skipped**, the identical pre-existing 11 names documented since Q275, 0 regressions.

**F. Build / publish.** `python3 scripts/regen_template_only.py all --out /dev/shm/q282_debug2 --src build/q265 --expect-changed index.html,nmsk-imaging-inline,nmsk-ultrasound-inline,clinical_needle_tool.js,clinical_imaging_tool.js,clinical_ultrasound_tool.js,parts_data.json,plexus_groups.json,symmetry_q237.json` -> `REGEN_TEMPLATE_ONLY_OK`, all six pages, every data block byte-identical (the clinical files themselves are untouched this round -- Quick view only reads `window.NMSKClinicalTool`, never modifies `clinical/needle_tool.js`). Published per page: `index.html` only (no clinical file changed, so none republished). **Final published versions**: Base M (HdYCRuvGP8ESbggoRWCNBF) v48->v49, Imaging M (RRkf5ELjmk6E8iHdgfbTtq) v125->v126, Imaging F (1nFD1WUQ7jyovz9vx9pn77) v112->v113, Combined M (FeFFPVVTEnPkDm2r7TyDFz) v49->v50, Combined F (1GEpFSCZexGZ1GnM1pXxuP) v60->v61, Base F (TiXsQe3eS5ehzN64Aozyth) v42->v43. **Still rough / honestly incomplete:** two of the nine actions in the new flow (picking the right structure from the search results, typing the numeric spacing) are irreducible real input, not panel-hopping, and were not counted as "friction" to eliminate. The orientation buttons set `cutCtl`'s internal `S.ori` to `"view"` (the generic custom-plane path `setFromSpec` always uses) rather than `"x"/"y"/"z"`, so the Cut panel's own orientation buttons will not show as visually "pressed" after using Quick view's axial/sagittal/coronal shortcuts even though the plane normal is numerically correct -- a cosmetic mismatch, not a functional one, not fixed this round. The abbreviated-labels checkbox always forces `text` to "abbr"/"full" and only touches `mode` when it was previously "off" -- it does not try to be a full mirror of the Labels panel's other settings (density, colour, callouts), which stays a separate, deliberately out-of-scope panel. ## Q283 (2026-10-25) -- NEW OWNER REQUEST: a "learn / explain" button for a structure, a muscle or a muscle group (chosen by text, on the model, or other ways), the choice highlighted and the rest semi-transparent (adjustable), a button to rotate the figure a half / full turn in a chosen direction, and a button to simulate the structure's action by moving the model -- owner's example: iliopsoas, psoas = hip flexion, iliacus = "adduction + flexion" (agent; published all six pages + hub + the owner's open-items page; UI + one cited derivation table, no geometry)

**A. Data, cited and checked.** (1) `data/anatomy/muscle_actions_q283.json` (new): the derivation table from free-text actions to Q241 pose-rig degrees of freedom -- 149 rows over 106 muscles, each row = one QUOTED action (verbatim substring of `data/muscles/<region>/<muscle>_r.json` `actions`, or of a quote in `cites`), the compartment it is limited to (`c`, e.g. `psoas_major`, `iliacus`, `long_head`, `anterior_1`; rows without `c` apply to the whole muscle and every part), and `mv` = [joint, dof, sign(, 1 = spine side-mirror)] in the rig's own sign convention (hip flex + / abd + / rot + = internal; ankle dp + = dorsiflexion; subtalar inv +; forearm sup +; wrist dev + = radial; spine regions lumbar/thoracic/cervical, lat/rot mirrored for left muscles). Every derivation choice that is not literal is a `note` on its row ("trunk" = lumbar + thoracic regions; head + neck = the rig's cervical region, which includes the occiput; toe/thumb motions put at the named joint; knee rotation / toe abduction not in the rig -> only the other part animated; "extends flexed humerus back to neutral" animated from flexion back to the model pose via `back`). `not_animated` records requested-but-uncited motions (iliacus adduction) and `none_lists` + `none_reasons` give every unmapped muscle its reason. One new citation: Kumazaki T, Takahashi T, Nakano T, Sakai T, Juntendo Iji Zasshi 2022;68(4):352-362, doi:10.14789/jmj.JMJ22-0009-OA (PMID 39021428, PMC11250012) -- a cadaveric moment-arm study treating psoas major and iliacus separately, both as hip flexors (quoted verbatim). (2) `data/anatomy/muscle_groups_q283.json` (new): 17 named textbook groups (quadriceps femoris, hamstrings, medial thigh adductors, gluteal, deep gluteal, triceps surae, anterior/lateral leg compartments, rotator cuff, thenar, hypothenar, erector spinae, anterolateral abdominal wall, scalenes, suboccipital, infra-/suprahyoid), source = the same Gray's Anatomy for Students / TA string the muscle files cite; functional groups ("hip flexion" etc.) are NOT stored -- derived at run time from the action table. (3) `scripts/anatomy/q283/build_learn.py` (new) builds `viewer/learn/learn_data.json` (193 KB: per muscle name/TA/origin/insertion/nerves+roots/actions verbatim/compartments/source + its rows) and FAILS on any quote that is not verbatim in its source, any unknown muscle/compartment/group member, any joint/dof absent from all six page rigs; `--check` for staleness. **Iliacus adduction: no citation found** -- the muscle file lists hip flexion only (Gray's), Kumazaki 2022 treats iliacus as a hip flexor, PubMed + web search on 2026-10-25 found no source for an iliacus adduction action (Song et al. 2020 J Biomech, doi:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2020.109968, only reports that iliacus ab/adduction moment arms differ between dysplastic and healthy hips -- not an action). So iliacus animates hip flexion only and its card says so verbatim ("Not animated for Iliacus: hip adduction. No citation found ...").

**B. Built: `viewer/learn/` (learn.html/.css/.js + learn_data.json), one shared module for both engines, synced by the new `scripts/sync_learn_q283.py` (css/html/js + the data as `<script type="application/json" id="nmsk-learn">`, `</` escaped).** `NMSKLearn(api)` on the same `anatomyApi()` object; `#t-learn` toolbar button (after Quick view); Quick view gained a "Learn" button that hands its pick over (`window.learnCtl.openFor(id)`). Search covers muscles present on this page (per side), their named parts, named groups and motions ("hip flexion" -> every muscle whose cited actions include it). Page structures are resolved to muscle/part by id (`<muscle>_<side>[_<part>]`, `zan_` prefix, and a unique-part-name index so `zan_psoas_major_r` -> iliopsoas/psoas_major); tendons/fascia/bursae excluded. Picking = highlight + fade others + camera: `selection().markIds(ids, true, true, true)` + `setGroup("sel","hl")` + `setGroup("oth","fade")` + `setFade(slider)` (Q227/Q232 verbatim; replaces the marks, Ctrl+Z undoes), `api.focus(bbox centre, max(160, 1.6 x extent))`. Follow mode (default on): while the panel is open, a click on a muscle on the model (the host's own selection, polled every 350 ms via a new `api.selectedId()`) opens it. Rotate: 4 one-click buttons (half / full turn x counter-clockwise / clockwise seen from above) via a new `api.orbit(dAzimuth)` (own engine: `az += d; place(); draw()`; Z engine: `cam.az += d; stopSpin(); need = true`). Simulate: each mapped row is a button (label generated from the motion, e.g. "Hip flexion", "Lumbar spine lateral flexion to its own side -- Psoas major"), with its quote, note and citation under it; "All together" merges the whole-muscle (+ chosen part) rows, dropping any dof the rows pull in opposite directions; groups/motions list aggregated motions ("Knee extension -- 4 muscles"). Animation = `api.pose().apply(pose)` per frame from the start pose: rest -> (pre-position to the opposite side when the target is < 8 deg away, e.g. knee extension from an extended knee) -> 70 % of the way to the cited range limit -> hold -> back, then `apply(start)` exactly; a virtual clock advances at most 350 ms per frame so slow devices still show every phase. A joint missing on this page's rig (e.g. no finger joints on the own-engine male) is skipped and named. No new camera, marking, highlighting or kinematics code.
